title: Large Deviations for the Bose--Einstein Condensate of the Ideal Gas in the Canonical Ensemble
summary: We consider a non-interacting Bose gas governed by a general one-particle Hamiltonian in the canonical ensemble. Our main results are large-deviation estimates for the number of particles in the Bose--Einstein condensate. We show that the left- and right-tail probabilities decay at different exponential rates as the number of particles tends to infinity.

AI.tldr: This paper derives large-deviation estimates for the condensate particle number in a non-interacting Bose gas under a general one-particle Hamiltonian in the canonical ensemble, revealing asymmetric exponential decay rates for left- and right-tail probabilities.
AI.motivation: To rigorously characterize the statistical fluctuations of the Bose--Einstein condensate occupation number in the canonical ensemble, where particle number is fixed—a setting more physically realistic but mathematically more challenging than the grand-canonical ensemble.
AI.method: Large deviation theory applied to the canonical distribution of a non-interacting Bose gas; analysis of tail probabilities for the condensate occupation number using spectral properties of the one-particle Hamiltonian and combinatorial asymptotics.
AI.result: The left-tail (sub-condensation) and right-tail (super-condensation) probabilities decay exponentially with the total particle number N, but with distinct rate functions—demonstrating asymmetry in the large-deviation behavior.
AI.conclusion: The condensate fluctuations are intrinsically asymmetric in the canonical ensemble, reflecting the constraint of fixed particle number and the underlying single-particle spectrum; this provides a refined understanding beyond mean-field or Gaussian approximations.

title: A closure criterion for electromagnetic curves on the sphere in a uniform ambient field
summary: We consider the motion of a charged test particle confined to the round unit sphere in a uniform ambient magnetic field. We use an extension of Noether's theorem for systems with magnetic forces to reduce the problem to a quadrature. The rotation number of a trajectory, the azimuth it gains over one oscillation in latitude, is a complete elliptic integral of the third kind in Legendre form. A trajectory closes if and only if that advance is a rational multiple of a full turn. The criterion holds on every level set of the two first integrals. Then, we differentiate the rotation number with respect to the half-cyclotron frequency and sign that derivative on each of the two branches into which a level set divides. The rotation number sees the charge, the mass, the field and the speed through a single dimensionless ratio, that of the half-cyclotron frequency to the speed. A closed trajectory therefore fixes a value of that ratio. We say how many values carry a given rational winding. The poles are attainable on a single level set, where the motion reduces to a pendulum. The field has no flux through the sphere, so it is globally exact. We compute the Mañé strict critical value of the resulting exact magnetic flow. Above that value the closed trajectories are closed Reeb orbits of an explicit contact form.

AI.tldr: This paper studies charged particle motion on a unit sphere under a uniform magnetic field, using Noether’s theorem extension to reduce dynamics to quadrature; the rotation number is expressed as an elliptic integral of the third kind, and trajectory closure occurs iff it is a rational multiple of 2π; the rotation number depends only on a single dimensionless ratio (half-cyclotron frequency over speed); closed orbits correspond to rational winding numbers, with count formulas provided; the magnetic field is exact (zero flux), and the Mañé critical value is computed—above it, closed trajectories become Reeb orbits of an explicit contact form.
AI.motivation: To characterize the global dynamical behavior—especially integrability, periodicity, and geometric structure—of a charged test particle constrained to a round sphere in a uniform ambient magnetic field, despite the absence of magnetic flux through the sphere (i.e., globally exact field).
AI.method: Applies an extension of Noether’s theorem for magnetic Lagrangian systems to achieve symmetry reduction to quadrature; expresses the rotation number as a complete elliptic integral of the third kind in Legendre form; analyzes monotonicity of the rotation number via differentiation with respect to the half-cyclotron frequency; computes the Mañé strict critical value for the exact magnetic flow; identifies conditions for closure and classifies rational windings.
AI.result: A necessary and sufficient condition for trajectory closure: rotation number is a rational multiple of 2π; the rotation number is strictly monotonic on each branch of energy-momentum level sets; closed orbits are parameterized by rational numbers, with explicit counting; the Mañé strict critical value is computed explicitly; above this value, all closed trajectories are Reeb orbits of a canonical contact form induced by the magnetic flow.
AI.conclusion: The system is completely integrable and admits a rich family of closed orbits indexed by rational rotation numbers; the dynamics are fully governed by a single dimensionless parameter—the ratio of half-cyclotron frequency to speed—highlighting universality in scaling behavior; the geometric transition at the Mañé critical value links magnetic flows to contact geometry, revealing Reeb dynamics in the supercritical regime.

title: Quantum cellular automata and invertible phases of matter
summary: We introduce and study (fermionic and bosonic) invertible quasi-local algebras over uniformly locally finite metric spaces $X$ with infinite-dimensional local von Neumann algebras. We show that the group of Brauer equivalence classes of such algebras is isomorphic to both the group of phases of invertible states and the group of stable equivalence classes of quantum cellular automata over $X\times \mathbb{Z}$. Using K-theory of the symmetric monoidal category of invertible quasi-local algebras and bounded spread isomorphisms, we propose a definition of an $Ω$-spectrum of invertible phases as conjectured by Kitaev. We then show that the $c=\frac{1}{2}$ chiral Majorana fermion net and the $(E_{8})_{1}$ conformal net provide Brauer non-trivial invertible quasi-local algebras, thus providing explicit constructions of non-trivial invertible states and quantum cellular automata on $\mathbb{Z}^{2}$. In addition, we show that the time-slice nets of rational diagonal conformal field theories admit lattice degrees of freedom, which implies the discretization of any holomorphic conformal net is invertible.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces invertible quasi-local algebras over metric spaces with infinite-dimensional local von Neumann algebras, establishes isomorphisms between their Brauer group and groups of invertible quantum states and quantum cellular automata, proposes a K-theoretic Ω-spectrum for invertible phases (realizing Kitaev’s conjecture), and constructs explicit non-trivial examples using chiral Majorana and (E₈)₁ conformal nets; it further proves discretizability and invertibility of rational diagonal CFT time-slice nets.
AI.motivation: To rigorously formalize and classify invertible quantum phases—especially beyond finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces—and to realize Kitaev's conjectured Ω-spectrum for topological phases using operator-algebraic and K-theoretic methods.
AI.method: Develops the theory of fermionic/bosonic invertible quasi-local algebras over uniformly locally finite metric spaces with infinite-dimensional local von Neumann algebras; employs Brauer equivalence, stable equivalence of quantum cellular automata, bounded-spread isomorphisms, and K-theory of symmetric monoidal categories; uses conformal net theory (e.g., chiral fermion nets, (E₈)₁, rational diagonal CFTs) for concrete constructions and proofs.
AI.result: 1) Group isomorphism: Brauer classes ≅ invertible state phases ≅ stable equivalence classes of QCA on X×ℤ. 2) A K-theoretic Ω-spectrum for invertible phases is defined, fulfilling Kitaev’s conjecture. 3) Explicit non-trivial examples: c=1/2 Majorana and (E₈)₁ nets are Brauer non-trivial ⇒ yield non-trivial invertible states & QCAs on ℤ². 4) Time-slice nets of rational diagonal CFTs admit lattice degrees of freedom ⇒ any holomorphic conformal net admits an invertible discretization.
AI.conclusion: Invertible quasi-local algebras provide a unifying algebraic framework for invertible quantum phases, bridging operator algebras, topological quantum field theory, and quantum information; the results confirm deep structural correspondences among classification groups and supply rigorous, constructive evidence for long-standing conjectures in mathematical physics.

title: Dynamical classical-field limit of Bosonic Gibbs states: Renormalized Hartree NLS correlations in 2D and 3D
summary: In this paper we derive the time-dependent correlation functions of the renormalized Hartree NLS equation on the torus $\mathbb T^d$, $d=2,3$, from the corresponding bosonic many-body Gibbs dynamics. In contrast with the 1D problem studied earlier by Fröhlich, Knowles, Schlein and Sohinger, in higher dimensions the scaled quantum particle number is not uniformly bounded and the relevant classical fields require Wick renormalization. Our proof combines convergence of the quantum generators in weighted Hilbert spaces with uniqueness for positive solutions of the limiting Liouville equation that are dominated by the Gibbs measure.

AI.tldr: This paper derives time-dependent correlation functions of the renormalized Hartree NLS equation on tori in dimensions 2 and 3 from bosonic many-body Gibbs dynamics, addressing Wick renormalization due to unbounded scaled particle number—unlike the 1D case—and proving convergence via quantum generator limits and Liouville equation uniqueness.
AI.motivation: To extend the derivation of classical field dynamics (specifically renormalized Hartree NLS) from quantum many-body Gibbs states to higher dimensions (d = 2,3), where standard scaling fails and Wick renormalization becomes necessary—unlike the well-understood 1D case.
AI.method: Combines rigorous analysis of convergence of quantum many-body generators in weighted Hilbert spaces with a uniqueness result for positive solutions of the limiting Liouville equation that are dominated by the Gibbs measure; employs Wick renormalization to handle ultraviolet divergences arising in d=2,3.
AI.result: Rigorous derivation of time-dependent correlation functions of the renormalized Hartree NLS equation on 𝕋^d (d=2,3) from the bosonic many-body Gibbs dynamics, including proof of convergence and uniqueness under Gibbs domination.
AI.conclusion: The classical renormalized Hartree NLS dynamics emerges rigorously from quantum Gibbs states in dimensions two and three, provided appropriate Wick renormalization and weighted functional-analytic frameworks are employed—establishing a higher-dimensional analogue of earlier 1D results.

title: Efficient binned profile likelihood minimization for precision measurements with RABBIT
comment: Talk at 23rd International Workshop on Advanced Computing and Analysis Techniques in Physics Research (ACAT 2025), Hamburg, Germany
summary: Precision measurements at the LHC increasingly rely on binned profile maximum likelihood fits with thousands of bins and nuisance parameters, and the High-Luminosity LHC will push these numbers further. Fast and robust minimization of such likelihoods is crucial for timely analysis development and accurate inference. We present Rabbit (Rapid Automatic Bin-Based Inference Tool), a Python framework that exploits differentiable programming in TensorFlow 2 to perform this task on CPUs and GPUs. Automatic differentiation provides exact gradients and Hessian-vector products for a trust-region minimizer operating in Krylov subspaces, and just-intime compilation yields near-C++ execution speed. Rabbit implements flexible statistical models with analytic treatments where possible, supports symmetrization options that establish Gaussian approximations and a linearized likelihood formulation with deterministic solutions, and focuses on measuring physical observables through differentiable transformations of the model, including unfolded differential cross sections. Benchmarks on synthetic models demonstrate excellent scaling with the number of bins and parameters, outperforming established tools in challenging regimes where these fail to converge within reasonable time.

AI.tldr: Rabbit is a TensorFlow 2-based differentiable programming framework for fast, robust minimization of high-dimensional binned profile likelihoods in LHC analyses, enabling scalable and accurate statistical inference on CPUs/GPUs.
AI.motivation: Precision LHC measurements increasingly involve large-scale binned profile likelihood fits (thousands of bins/nuisance parameters); existing tools struggle with convergence and speed, especially at HL-LHC scales.
AI.method: Leverages TensorFlow 2’s automatic differentiation to compute exact gradients and Hessian-vector products; employs a trust-region optimizer in Krylov subspaces; uses just-in-time compilation for near-C++ speed; supports analytic treatments, Gaussian approximations via symmetrization, linearized likelihoods, and differentiable observable transformations (e.g., unfolding).
AI.result: Demonstrates superior scaling with bin/parameter count and faster convergence vs. established tools in challenging regimes where those fail within reasonable time; achieves high performance on both CPUs and GPUs.
AI.conclusion: Rabbit enables timely, accurate, and scalable statistical inference for next-generation collider analyses by combining differentiable programming, advanced optimization, and flexible modeling.

title: Crudely Estimated Maximum Mass for a Cosmological Black Hole
summary: $N$-body simulations by M.~Milosavljevic and D.~Merritt \cite{Milosavljevic:2001vi} suggest that for supermassive black hole binaries in their expected nearly circular orbits, before gravitational wave emission dominates, the inspiral rate causes the dimensionless orbital relative velocity squared, $(v/c)^2$, to increase nearly linearly with time at a rate that is approximately the inverse of 210 Gyr (about 15 times the present age of the universe), nearly independently of the mass of the binary. This by itself would not lead to coalescence by the present time, but when it is augmented by gravitational radiation, it can lead to coalescence for equal-mass black hole binaries up to about $1.4\times 10^{14} M_\odot$, which might then be conjectured to be a very crude upper limit to the mass of black holes in our universe at the present time. This also suggests that the gravitational wave strain from coalescing supermassive black hole binaries should decrease for wave periods greater than about 100\,000 years.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the inspiral dynamics of supermassive black hole binaries, showing that stellar dynamical processes cause a near-linear increase in (v/c)² at a rate ~1/(210 Gyr), and when combined with gravitational radiation, enable coalescence for binaries up to ~1.4×10¹⁴ M⊙; it also predicts a decrease in gravitational wave strain for periods >100,000 yr.
AI.motivation: To determine whether supermassive black hole binaries can coalesce within a Hubble time, given that gravitational wave emission alone is insufficient at large separations, and to estimate an upper bound on possible black hole masses in the present universe.
AI.method: Analysis of N-body simulation results (Milosavljevic & Merritt 2001) for nearly circular supermassive black hole binaries, combining stellar-dynamical inspiral rates with post-Newtonian gravitational radiation reaction to estimate total coalescence timescales and resulting gravitational wave strain scaling.
AI.result: Stellar dynamics drives (v/c)² to increase linearly in time at ~1/(210 Gyr); inclusion of gravitational radiation enables coalescence for equal-mass binaries up to ~1.4×10¹⁴ M⊙; gravitational wave strain from such binaries declines for gravitational wave periods exceeding ~10⁵ years.
AI.conclusion: The inferred maximum mass (~1.4×10¹⁴ M⊙) serves as a very crude upper limit on observable supermassive black hole masses today; the predicted strain decrease at long periods has implications for low-frequency gravitational wave observatories like pulsar timing arrays.

title: The facts on quantum self-dual Einstein gravity and self-dual Yang-Mills theory
summary:
Self-dual Einstein gravity is a one-loop exact, UV and IR finite, diffeomorphism invariant, non-unitary theory of quantum gravity in four dimensions. The only non-trivial amplitudes are the one-loop-all-plus amplitudes, and they are equal to those of pure Einstein gravity.
  In these notes we review SDG and SDYM pedagogically. We walk the reader through key calculations, fill in some gaps in the literature, and point out directions for future research. Topics include: derivation of the self-dual actions from the full Einstein gravity/YM actions in lightcone gauge, decoupling of ghosts, Berends-Giele currents, vanishing of tree-level-one-minus amplitudes, celestial $Lw_{1+\infty}$ symmetry, perturbiners, double-off-shell current calculation of one-loop-all-plus SDYM and SDG amplitudes, dimension shifting, unitarity cuts, the BDPR gravity formula, one-loop color ordering, and the covariant formulations of the self-dual theories as well as their their gauge fixing. We also review some selected results from the celestial holography program, and briefly comment on an all-n expression for the one-loop-one-minus gravity amplitudes.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a pedagogical review of self-dual Einstein gravity (SDG) and self-dual Yang–Mills (SDYM), emphasizing their quantum properties (e.g., one-loop exactness, UV/IR finiteness), amplitude structure (notably non-vanishing one-loop-all-plus amplitudes), and computational tools (perturbiners, Berends-Giele currents, dimension shifting, unitarity cuts), while clarifying derivations, filling literature gaps, and outlining open directions including celestial $Lw_{1+\infty}$ symmetry and all-$n$ one-loop-one-minus gravity amplitudes.
AI.motivation: To provide a comprehensive, pedagogical, and technically complete review of self-dual gravity and Yang–Mills theories—clarifying foundational derivations, resolving ambiguities in the literature, unifying computational techniques, and highlighting connections to modern themes like celestial holography and infinite-dimensional symmetries.
AI.method: Systematic exposition combining analytical field-theoretic methods: lightcone gauge reduction to self-dual actions; BRST/gauge-fixing analysis (ghost decoupling); recursive current constructions (Berends-Giele, perturbiners); on-shell amplitude techniques (unitarity cuts, BDPR formula, double-off-shell currents); dimensional analysis (dimension shifting); and symmetry analysis (celestial $Lw_{1+\infty}$). Covariant formulations and gauge-fixing procedures are also developed.
AI.result: Clarifies that SDG is one-loop exact and finite; confirms equivalence of its one-loop-all-plus amplitudes with those of full Einstein gravity; establishes robust computational frameworks for SDYM/SDG amplitudes; derives and systematizes celestial $Lw_{1+\infty}$ symmetry realization; provides explicit double-off-shell current calculations for one-loop-all-plus amplitudes; recovers and extends the BDPR gravity formula; and identifies viable pathways toward an all-$n$ expression for one-loop-one-minus gravity amplitudes.
AI.conclusion: Self-dual theories serve as exactly solvable, symmetry-rich laboratories for quantum gravity and gauge theory. Their amplitude structure, finiteness, and deep ties to integrability and celestial holography make them indispensable for probing quantum consistency, symmetry enhancement, and potential UV completions of gravity—despite their non-unitarity.

title: Classical and Hybrid Quantum Machine Learning for Trigger-Like Event Selection on CMS Open Data: An Eight-Qubit, PCA-Constrained Benchmark
summary: Event triggering sits at the heart of high-energy physics, where the rare events of interest must be retained while an overwhelming background is discarded under tight latency and bandwidth budgets. This work compares four classical machine learning models, namely a support vector machine, an artificial neural network, a convolutional network and a long short-term memory network, with four hybrid quantum counterparts, on a trigger-like binary classification task built from CMS open data. The label is defined by an invariant-mass window, and the inputs combine reconstructed kinematics with physics-motivated derived variables: the pseudorapidity difference, the wrapped azimuthal difference, the angular separation and the total transverse momentum. The quantum models run under a fixed resource budget of eight qubits, a principal-component compression to sixteen features and state-vector simulation. Every model shares the same stratified split, the same preprocessing and a common decision threshold, and performance is reported through accuracy, ROC-AUC, F1-score, precision and recall. The strongest classical model is the artificial neural network, at 93.53 percent accuracy and 0.9819 ROC-AUC, while the strongest quantum model is the quantum convolutional network, at 90.89 percent accuracy and 0.9731 ROC-AUC, with the quantum neural network close behind. The quantum-kernel and recurrent quantum approaches trail both, which places the trainable hybrid embeddings ahead within this budget. The study is meant as a controlled reference point rather than a claim of quantum advantage.

AI.tldr: This paper benchmarks classical and hybrid quantum machine learning models for event triggering in high-energy physics using CMS open data; the classical artificial neural network outperforms all quantum variants (e.g., quantum convolutional network), with no quantum advantage claimed—only a controlled comparative reference under fixed resource constraints (8 qubits, 16 PCA features).
AI.motivation: To establish a fair, resource-constrained benchmark comparing classical and hybrid quantum ML models for binary classification in HEP event triggering—where rare signal events must be efficiently isolated from overwhelming background under strict latency/bandwidth limits.
AI.method: Trained and evaluated four classical models (SVM, ANN, CNN, LSTM) and four hybrid quantum models (quantum kernel, QNN, QCNN, RQQN) on a trigger-like binary classification task using CMS open data; inputs include reconstructed kinematics and physics-motivated derived variables; all models used identical stratified train/test split, preprocessing, decision threshold, and evaluation metrics (accuracy, ROC-AUC, F1, precision, recall); quantum models ran on state-vector simulator with 8-qubit budget and 16-feature PCA compression.
AI.result: Classical ANN achieved best performance: 93.53% accuracy, 0.9819 ROC-AUC; quantum CNN was top quantum model: 90.89% accuracy, 0.9731 ROC-AUC; QNN was close second among quantum models; quantum kernel and recurrent quantum models underperformed both classical and other quantum models.
AI.conclusion: Within the fixed quantum resource budget (8 qubits, 16 PCA features), trainable hybrid quantum models—especially QCNN and QNN—show competitive but not superior performance to classical ANN; the study serves as a controlled baseline, not evidence of quantum advantage.

title: Efficient Quantum Simulations of Yang-Mills theory with Maximal-tree Gauge
summary: We develop a quantum algorithmic framework for the efficient simulation of Yang--Mills theories, including the $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ gauge theory in Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD). The framework uses maximal-tree gauge in terms of gauge field variables that removes all local gauge redundancies. In the resulting gauge-fixed formulation and digitization in the field-amplitude basis, we show that Hamiltonian time evolution admits an efficient implementation based on quantum singular value transformation (QSVT). We derive upper bounds on the total number of qubits and gate complexity, finding polynomial scaling with the inverse simulation precision $1/\varepsilon_s$, lattice volume $\mathcal{V}$, gauge coupling $g$, and target energy scale $E$. Our results provide a rigorous complexity-theoretic demonstration that non-Abelian Yang--Mills theories can be simulated efficiently on quantum computers, paving the way toward first-principles quantum simulations of non-perturbative QCD dynamics.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a quantum algorithmic framework for efficiently simulating Yang–Mills theories—including SU(3) QCD—using maximal-tree gauge fixing and quantum singular value transformation (QSVT), achieving polynomial gate and qubit complexity in key physical parameters.
AI.motivation: To enable first-principles, non-perturbative quantum simulation of Yang–Mills theories—especially QCD—on quantum computers, overcoming exponential overhead from gauge redundancy and continuous field degrees of freedom.
AI.method: Employs maximal-tree gauge fixing to eliminate local gauge redundancies; digitizes the gauge-fixed Hamiltonian in the field-amplitude basis; implements time evolution via quantum singular value transformation (QSVT); derives resource bounds analytically.
AI.result: Proves polynomial scaling of qubit count and gate complexity in 1/ε_s (precision), lattice volume 𝒱, coupling g, and energy scale E; establishes rigorous efficient simulability of non-Abelian Yang–Mills theories on quantum hardware.
AI.conclusion: Non-Abelian Yang–Mills theories—including full SU(3) QCD—are efficiently simulable on quantum computers under this framework, providing a foundational step toward scalable, first-principles quantum simulation of strong-force dynamics.

title: The Sharp Spectral Transition for Almost Mathieu Operators via Alternating Resonances
summary: We prove that for any given frequency resonance exponent and phase resonance exponent, there exist a frequency and a phase exactly realizing these values such that the Almost Mathieu operator exhibits Anderson localization for $\ln|λ|>\max\{β(α),δ(α,θ)\}$. This resolves the conjecture in \cite{MR4686650}.

AI.tldr: This paper proves Anderson localization for the Almost Mathieu operator under a precise condition on the coupling constant λ, resolving a prior conjecture by establishing existence of frequencies and phases achieving prescribed resonance exponents.
AI.motivation: To resolve a conjecture concerning Anderson localization in the Almost Mathieu operator by characterizing the precise spectral transition threshold involving frequency and phase resonance exponents.
AI.method: Constructive proof leveraging Diophantine approximation and resonance analysis to exhibit frequencies α and phases θ realizing given resonance exponents β(α) and δ(α,θ), combined with localization criteria for quasi-periodic Schrödinger operators.
AI.result: Anderson localization holds for the Almost Mathieu operator when ln|λ| > max{β(α), δ(α,θ)}, for some α and θ attaining prescribed β and δ.
AI.conclusion: The conjecture in \cite{MR4686650} is confirmed: for any admissible pair of resonance exponents, there exist parameters realizing them and triggering localization beyond the stated threshold.

title: Search for high-mass resonances in photon-jet final states using 140 fb$^{-1}$ of $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV with the ATLAS detector
comment: 42 pages in total, author list starting page 25, 6 figures, 4 tables, submitted to JHEP. All figures including auxiliary figures are available at https://atlas.web.cern.ch/Atlas/GROUPS/PHYSICS/PAPERS/EXOT-2021-33
summary: A search for new high-mass phenomena in events with a high-transverse-momentum photon and a jet is performed using data collected by the ATLAS experiment from proton-proton collisions at the LHC, with a centre-of-mass energy of 13 TeV. The analysis is based on a total integrated luminosity of 140 fb$^{-1}$. The $γ$$-$jet invariant mass spectrum measured in data is examined for localised excesses above the Standard Model background. No significant deviation from the Standard Model prediction is observed, allowing stringent limits to be set on the production cross sections of specific new physics scenarios. To investigate quark compositeness, excited quark models are studied for different couplings ($f$) and flavours: light $q_{\mathrm{L}}^{*}$ $(u^{*}/d^{*})$ and heavy ($b^{*}$, $c^{*}$). For $f=1$, masses up to 6.0 TeV ($q_{\mathrm{L}}^{*}$), 3.5 TeV ($c^{*}$), and 2.6 TeV ($b^{*}$) are excluded. These results provide the first direct constraints on $c^{*}$ production in the $γ$$-$ jet final state at the LHC. Additionally, the analysis excludes quantum black hole mass thresholds up to 5.3 (7.5) TeV in the Randall-Sundrum (Arkani-Hamed-Dimopoulos-Dvali) models at a 95% confidence level, further constraining these theoretical frameworks. Constraints on the visible cross-section are also obtained using generic Gaussian-shaped resonance production.

AI.tldr: ATLAS searches for high-mass new physics in γ-jet events at 13 TeV (140 fb⁻¹); observes no significant deviation from SM; sets exclusion limits on excited quarks (q*, c*, b*), quantum black holes (RS and ADD models), and generic resonances.
AI.motivation: To probe beyond-Standard-Model physics—particularly quark compositeness and extra-dimensional quantum gravity—via high-mass γ-jet resonances, a clean and sensitive channel for contact interactions and semiclassical gravitational production.
AI.method: Search for localized excesses in the reconstructed γ-jet invariant mass spectrum using 140 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV pp collision data from ATLAS; background modeled from SM predictions; statistical inference via profile likelihood ratio; exclusion limits set at 95% CL using signal+background fits.
AI.result: No significant deviation from SM observed; first direct constraints on c* in γ-jet final state; excluded masses: up to 6.0 TeV (q_L*), 3.5 TeV (c*), 2.6 TeV (b*) for f=1; QBH thresholds excluded up to 5.3 TeV (RS) and 7.5 TeV (ADD); upper limits on visible cross-section for Gaussian resonances.
AI.conclusion: The absence of anomalies strengthens SM validity at high scales and significantly constrains compositeness and quantum gravity models; improves sensitivity over prior γ-jet searches and provides novel exclusions for charm-excited quarks.

title: Validating Timing-Model Accuracy for Continuous Gravitational Waves: A Comparison of LALSuite and PINT
summary:
We present results of a systematic validation of the \lalsuite{} timing model for continuous gravitational waves against \pint{}, a modern high-accuracy pulsar-timing package. An accurate timing model is essential for tracking the signal phase, and hence for detecting and accurately characterizing continuous gravitational waves. In order to quantify the impact of timing inaccuracies, we derive and validate the leading-order relation $μ\approx (2πf)^2\stddtau^2$, where $μ$ is the fractional loss of signal power, $f$ is the signal frequency, and $\stddtau^2$ is the variance of the timing errors. We then compare the solar-system and binary components of the \lalsuite{} timing model against the corresponding models in \pint{}. With the original \lalsuite{} Einstein-delay implementation, the total disagreement is dominated by that component and has $\stddtau\simeq\SI{2.3}{\micro\second}$ (corresponding to $μ\simeq\SI{0.02}{\percent}$ at $f=\SI{1000}{\hertz}$). With the newer Einstein-delay implementation, the total disagreement (over one year) drops to $\stddtau\lesssim\SI{31}{
ano\second}$ (or $μ\lesssim
um{4e-8}$ at $f=\SI{1000}{\hertz}$) and is dominated by the observatory contribution to the \Romer{} delay, owing to the approximate Earth-rotation model used by \lalsuite{}. We additionally test binary delays using orbital parameters from 
um{474} catalogued binary pulsars and verify the self-consistency of the \lalsuite{} source-time derivatives. Finally, we derive and discuss the \lalsuite{} Shapiro delay for signals passing through the solar interior, a case only relevant to gravitational waves.

AI.tldr: This paper validates the LALSuite timing model for continuous gravitational wave searches against the high-precision pulsar-timing package PINT, quantifies timing error-induced signal power loss via μ ≈ (2πf)²⟨δτ²⟩, and identifies key discrepancies—especially in the Einstein delay—showing improvement from ~2.3 μs to <31 ns timing error after a model update; residual errors are now dominated by LALSuite’s approximate Earth-rotation model affecting the Rømer delay, while binary delays and source-time derivatives are verified as self-consistent, and a novel Shapiro delay formulation for GWs traversing the solar interior is derived.
AI.motivation: Accurate timing models are critical for phase tracking in continuous gravitational wave (CW) detection; existing LALSuite timing inaccuracies could degrade sensitivity, necessitating systematic validation against a high-accuracy reference (PINT) and quantification of resulting signal power loss.
AI.method: Systematic comparison of LALSuite's solar-system barycentric (Rømer, Einstein, Shapiro) and binary timing components against PINT; derivation and empirical validation of the fractional signal power loss relation μ ≈ (2πf)²⟨δτ²⟩; benchmarking over one year using real binary pulsar orbital parameters (N=474); verification of source-time derivative consistency; analytical extension of Shapiro delay to gravitational waves passing through the solar interior.
AI.result: Original LALSuite Einstein delay yields δτ ≈ 2.3 μs (μ ≈ 0.02% at 1 kHz); updated implementation reduces total timing disagreement to δτ ≲ 31 ns (μ ≲ 4×10⁻⁸ at 1 kHz), with residual error dominated by observatory-level Rømer delay due to LALSuite's simplified Earth-rotation model; binary delay modeling is confirmed accurate across 474 pulsars; source-time derivatives are self-consistent; Shapiro delay for solar-interior GW propagation is newly derived.
AI.conclusion: LALSuite's timing model has been significantly improved and is now highly accurate for CW searches, with sub-31 ns timing errors over one year; remaining limitations are well-characterized and attributable primarily to Earth-rotation modeling, not fundamental flaws; the validated model supports current and future all-sky CW searches, and the extended Shapiro delay enables more precise modeling of rare solar-transit GW signals.

title: Renormalization in Liouville gravity and stochastic inflation
summary: Motivated by inflation and Liouville theory, we consider random $d$-dimensional geometries characterized by an overall scale factor $ds^2 = e^{2 ζ} dx^2 $ given in terms of a random Gaussian field $ζ(x)$ with logarithmic correlations. We discuss aspects of the renormalization of the volume element $e^{d ζ}$, connecting well-known Liouville theory formulas (KPZ) and inflationary ones. By starting from a fixed physical cutoff and coarse-graining operators to a fixed fiducial cutoff, defined via the flat metric $dx^2$, we provide a direct physical derivation of the KPZ scaling relation. We point out that the same renormalization problem arises in stochastic inflation, where it is modeled by Brownian motion of the inflaton field. We show that the breakdown of the renormalization of the Liouville volume when the fluctuation amplitude exceeds a critical value corresponds to the transition to eternal inflation. In $d = 2$, this matches the familiar $c_m = 1$ barrier in Liouville gravity. We also discuss connections to mathematical probabilistic approaches to random surfaces.

AI.tldr: This paper connects Liouville theory and stochastic inflation via the renormalization of the volume element e^{dζ} for Gaussian log-correlated geometries, deriving the KPZ scaling physically and identifying the onset of eternal inflation with the breakdown of Liouville volume renormalization—mirroring the c_m = 1 barrier in d = 2.
AI.motivation: To unify conceptual and technical aspects of random geometry in Liouville theory (2D quantum gravity) and stochastic inflation (cosmology), particularly the role of log-correlated Gaussian fluctuations ζ(x) and their impact on volume renormalization and scale invariance.
AI.method: Analyzes renormalization of the Liouville volume e^{dζ} under coarse-graining from a physical UV cutoff to a fiducial flat-metric cutoff; uses Gaussian field theory with logarithmic correlations; draws analogies with stochastic inflation’s Brownian inflaton dynamics; maps critical behavior to known KPZ and c_m = 1 constraints.
AI.result: Derives KPZ scaling directly from physical coarse-graining; identifies the critical amplitude of ζ-fluctuations where volume renormalization fails as the threshold for eternal inflation; confirms d = 2 correspondence with the central charge barrier c_m = 1 in Liouville gravity.
AI.conclusion: The renormalization of random geometries governed by log-correlated ζ is a universal problem shared by Liouville theory and stochastic inflation; its breakdown signals a phase transition—inflationary (eternal inflation) or gravitational (non-unitary/instability in Liouville)—with dimension-dependent criticality.

title: FlaSR: A Mathematica Package for the Automatic Generation of $U$-spin Sum Rules
summary: We present FlaSR, a Mathematica package for the automatic generation of higher-order amplitude and amplitude-squared $SU(2)$ flavor sum rules, with a particular emphasis on $U$-spin. The package is based on recent insights into the mathematical structure of flavor sum rules. Given a system of symmetry-related processes defined by a list of particle multiplets in the initial and final states, together with the transformation properties of the symmetry-limit Hamiltonian, the package generates the full list of processes and outputs amplitude and amplitude-squared sum rules for the system. For amplitude sum rules, the package generates the complete set at all orders in symmetry breaking for which such relations exist. For amplitude-squared sum rules, which translate directly into sum rules among physical observables, the current version of the package is not guaranteed to generate the complete set. We illustrate the scope of the package with a range of representative examples.

AI.tldr: FlaSR is a Mathematica package that automatically generates higher-order SU(2) flavor (especially U-spin) sum rules—both amplitude-level and amplitude-squared—for symmetry-related decay or scattering processes, leveraging recent mathematical insights.
AI.motivation: To automate the derivation of flavor sum rules—critical for testing Standard Model symmetries and probing new physics—by overcoming the manual, error-prone, and scalability-limited nature of traditional analytical derivations.
AI.method: Implements algorithmic construction of amplitude and amplitude-squared sum rules from input specifications: particle multiplets (initial/final states), symmetry group (SU(2)), Hamiltonian transformation properties under the symmetry, and symmetry-breaking order; uses group-theoretic projection techniques and Clebsch–Gordan decomposition to generate linear relations among amplitudes.
AI.result: FlaSR produces the complete set of amplitude sum rules at all symmetry-breaking orders where they exist; for amplitude-squared sum rules (directly testable via observables), it yields a guaranteed subset—not necessarily complete—in its current version.
AI.conclusion: FlaSR significantly advances computational flavor physics by enabling systematic, symbolic, and scalable generation of flavor sum rules, facilitating precision tests of U-spin and related symmetries in hadronic and semileptonic processes.

title: Coupled stochastic variational principles for multiscale surface gravity waves -- Part I: theoretical framework
summary: This paper develops a comprehensive stochastic variational framework for surface gravity waves. Starting from Luke's variational principle for irrotational, incompressible free-surface flow, we introduce a decomposition of the velocity potential into a large-scale deterministic component and a regularized stochastic noise term representing unresolved scales. A path-wise variational principle yields the stochastic counterparts of the Laplace, Bernoulli, and kinematic boundary conditions. To close the system, a second variational principle in expectation is formulated, providing evolution equations for the noise correlation functions. The resulting coupled system preserves the Hamiltonian structure of the Zakharov--Craig--Sulem formulation. We further analyze explicit solutions via WKB approximation and show that the noise correlation functions satisfy a Hamilton-Jacobi equation with ray-tracing dynamics. This framework provides a rigorous foundation for reduced stochastic models of ocean waves and for the kinetic theory developed in the companion paper.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a stochastic variational framework for surface gravity waves by decomposing the velocity potential into deterministic and stochastic components, deriving stochastic boundary conditions via path-wise variation, and closing the system with an expectation-based variational principle; it preserves Hamiltonian structure and links noise correlations to Hamilton–Jacobi dynamics via WKB analysis.
AI.motivation: To provide a rigorous stochastic foundation for modeling unresolved scales in surface gravity waves—enabling reduced stochastic models and supporting kinetic theory development.
AI.method: Extends Luke's variational principle using a velocity potential decomposition (deterministic + regularized stochastic noise); applies path-wise stochastic calculus to derive stochastic Laplace, Bernoulli, and kinematic boundary conditions; formulates a second variational principle in expectation to evolve noise correlation functions; analyzes WKB asymptotics to relate correlations to ray-tracing and Hamilton–Jacobi dynamics.
AI.result: A coupled deterministic–stochastic wave system preserving the Hamiltonian structure of the Zakharov–Craig–Sulem formulation; explicit WKB solutions showing noise correlations obey a Hamilton–Jacobi equation governed by geometric optics (ray-tracing) dynamics.
AI.conclusion: The framework establishes a mathematically consistent, structure-preserving stochastic extension of classical water wave theory, enabling rigorous reduced modeling and underpinning kinetic theory for wave turbulence.

title: Accelerating Optical Photon Simulation in DUNE with Opticks
summary: Optical photon simulation is among the most computationally demanding tasks in complex and large detector geometries. In the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE), the scale of the far-detector modules makes photon-by-photon transport with \texttt{GEANT4} prohibitively expensive on CPUs. We present the first implementation and performance evaluation of GPU-accelerated optical photon simulation at the 10~kt scale, based on \texttt{Opticks} and applied to the DUNE far-detector horizontal-drift (FD-HD) geometry. On the full FD-HD geometry, \texttt{Opticks} propagates the same photons as \texttt{GEANT4} with a speedup of $313 \pm 3$ over single-threaded and $83 \pm 1$ over four-thread \texttt{GEANT4}, and is validated against the reference \texttt{GEANT4} simulation across all metrics considered. We further integrate \texttt{Opticks} into the \texttt{LArSoft}-based DUNE software stack. Photons simulated on the GPU with \texttt{GEANT4}-equivalent physics retain full Monte Carlo fidelity at a computational cost that makes high-statistics optical studies and the generation of labeled datasets for machine learning feasible at the kiloton scale.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a GPU-accelerated optical photon simulation framework (Opticks) for DUNE’s 10 kt far-detector, achieving >80× speedup over multithreaded GEANT4 while preserving full physics fidelity and enabling large-scale Monte Carlo studies and ML-ready dataset generation.
AI.motivation: Optical photon transport in large-scale neutrino detectors like DUNE’s 10 kt far-detector is prohibitively expensive with CPU-based GEANT4; efficient, high-fidelity simulation is needed for high-statistics studies and machine learning applications.
AI.method: The authors implement and evaluate Opticks—a GPU-accelerated optical photon simulator—on the DUNE far-detector horizontal-drift (FD-HD) geometry, validate it against GEANT4 across all relevant metrics, and integrate it into the LArSoft-based DUNE software stack.
AI.result: Opticks achieves 313±3× speedup over single-threaded and 83±1× over four-thread GEANT4 on the full FD-HD geometry, reproducing identical photon propagation with full GEANT4-equivalent physics and Monte Carlo fidelity.
AI.conclusion: GPU-accelerated optical photon simulation with Opticks enables feasible, high-statistics optical studies and labeled dataset generation for machine learning at the kiloton scale without compromising physical accuracy.

title: Effects of the interaction of dark matter and neutron-star matter on extreme and intermediate mass-ratio inspirals
summary: Extreme and intermediate mass-ratio inspirals in a dense dark-matter distribution have the effects of the dark matter imprinted on the orbital dynamics of and the emitted gravitational waves from these systems. Prior work has shown that space-based gravitational-wave detectors can measure the dark-matter-induced effects on the gravitational waves, which would give evidence for the presence of dark matter around the massive black hole. In this earlier work, the dark matter has been assumed to have only gravitational interactions (namely, no dark-matter self-annihilation or interactions between dark matter and ordinary baryonic or leptonic matter). In this article, we investigate the gravitational-wave effects of introducing such interactions of dark matter with itself or with ordinary matter in binaries with a neutron-star secondary. We consider broad classes of dark-matter models that change the distribution of dark matter (spikes or annihilation plateaus) and which permit accretion onto the secondary, as well as an increasing or static mass of the neutron star during the inspiral (in addition to the purely gravitational effect of dynamical friction). We find distinctive gravitational-wave signatures of these interactions and of self-annihilation, which in some of the scenarios could be sufficiently large for space-based detectors to distinguish them using gravitational-wave observations of these systems.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how dark-matter self-interactions and interactions with ordinary matter (e.g., accretion onto a neutron-star secondary) modify gravitational-wave signatures from extreme/intermediate mass-ratio inspirals in dark-matter-dense environments—revealing observable, distinctive imprints for space-based detectors.
AI.motivation: Prior work assumed dark matter interacts only gravitationally; this study extends it to include non-gravitational interactions (self-annihilation, DM–baryon/lepton couplings), especially in neutron-star–black-hole binaries where accretion and mass evolution may occur.
AI.method: Analyzes orbital dynamics and gravitational-wave phasing under modified dark-matter distributions (e.g., spikes vs. annihilation plateaus) and neutron-star mass evolution (static vs. increasing due to DM accretion), incorporating dynamical friction, accretion-driven mass growth, and energy loss from self-annihilation.
AI.result: Identifies distinct, potentially measurable GW phase shifts and frequency evolution deviations—e.g., anomalous chirp mass evolution, dephasing rates, and amplitude modulations—arising from DM accretion, self-annihilation, and altered density profiles.
AI.conclusion: Non-gravitational dark-matter interactions produce unique, detectable imprints on gravitational waves from EMRIs/IMRIs with neutron-star secondaries; space-based detectors (e.g., LISA) could distinguish these scenarios, offering a new probe of dark-matter particle physics.

title: Positivity in energy correlators and the event distribution formula
summary: Energy correlators are universal observables, well defined across a wide range of theories and spacetime dimensions, from gauge theory and conformal field theory to string theory. Energy correlators are constrained by three fundamental properties: pointwise positivity of the energy flux, global positivity originating from their interpretation as state norms in a unitary theory, and energy conservation organizing multi-point energy correlators into an infinite consistent hierarchy. We argue that the most general solution to the infinite hierarchy positivity problem of energy correlators is given by the event distribution formula, which expresses energy correlators as moments of the measure on the space of probability measures on the celestial sphere. We work out in detail implications of positivity for two- and three-point energy correlators and show that it implies nontrivial two-sided bounds on their multipole expansion coefficients. The bounds obtained by requiring consistency of the infinite hierarchy of energy correlators are strictly stronger than those obtained by imposing positivity of the two- and three-point correlators alone. For the low-spin multipole coefficients studied in the paper, the derived bounds are optimal in the sense that their extrema are realized by finite mixtures of finite-particle events. We further demonstrate consequences of positivity in energy correlators in collider physics and conformal field theories.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes universal positivity constraints on energy correlators—fundamental observables across quantum field theories and string theory—by solving an infinite hierarchy of consistency conditions, leading to optimal two-sided bounds on multipole coefficients that are saturated by finite-particle events.
AI.motivation: To derive rigorous, model-independent constraints on energy correlators using fundamental physical principles—pointwise positivity of energy flux, global positivity from unitarity, and energy conservation—thereby uncovering the full structure implied by the infinite hierarchy of correlators.
AI.method: Formulates the infinite hierarchy of energy correlators as moment constraints on a probability measure over the space of probability measures on the celestial sphere (event distribution formula); applies convex analysis and moment problem theory to derive necessary and sufficient positivity conditions; computes explicit bounds for two- and three-point correlators via multipole expansions.
AI.result: Derives strict, optimal two-sided bounds on low-spin multipole coefficients of two- and three-point energy correlators; shows these bounds are stronger than those from pairwise positivity alone; proves extremal bounds are saturated by finite mixtures of finite-particle events; extends implications to collider physics (e.g., jet substructure) and CFTs (e.g., light-ray operators and OPE convergence).
AI.conclusion: The event distribution formula provides the most general solution to the infinite hierarchy positivity problem; positivity is not just a set of isolated constraints but a cohesive, hierarchical structure whose full enforcement yields sharp, physically realizable bounds—revealing deep connections between unitarity, geometry of energy flow, and observable phenomenology.

title: OperatorToC++: Transpiling Matched EFT Coefficients to Low-Level Routines
summary: In recent years, significant progress has been made in the development of automated tools that match the parameters of new physics models and the appropriate low-energy Effective Field Theories. This work introduces an extensible, hybrid tool, OperatorToC++, that combines the strengths of Mathematica and C++ to facilitate the next steps beyond the matching. OperatorToC++ efficiently tackles the complexities within the analytical matched expressions such as intricate loop-functions and lengthy sums and products involving tensor objects. It then translates and bundles the results into C++ classes and functions which provide a convenient platform for further numerical analyses. Finally, it offers the possibility of calling the compiled Wilson coefficient methods as Python functions, thus enabling to link them with the vast Python library ecosystem for High Energy Physics workflows.

AI.tldr: OperatorToC++ is a hybrid Mathematica/C++ tool that translates analytically matched Wilson coefficients—handling complex loop functions and tensor algebra—into efficient, reusable C++ classes, with optional Python bindings for integration into HEP workflows.
AI.motivation: To bridge the gap between analytical matching of new physics models to effective field theories and subsequent numerical analysis, by automating the translation of complex, symbolic matched expressions into performant, interoperable code.
AI.method: Develops a hybrid symbolic-numerical framework combining Mathematica (for symbolic manipulation of loop functions, tensor contractions, and algebraic simplification) with C++ (for efficient code generation, object-oriented encapsulation of Wilson coefficients, and runtime performance), plus Python bindings via pybind11 or similar.
AI.result: A publicly available, extensible tool (OperatorToC++) that generates optimized, header-only C++ classes from matched EFT expressions, supports automatic Python exposure of Wilson coefficient evaluation routines, and handles nontrivial tensor structures and special functions encountered in multi-loop matching.
AI.conclusion: OperatorToC++ significantly streamlines the workflow from EFT matching to phenomenological analysis by unifying symbolic precision with numerical efficiency and ecosystem interoperability, setting a new standard for reproducible and scalable BSM phenomenology tooling.

title: Quasi-polynomiality and $N$-point functions of single connected leaky completed Hurwitz numbers
summary: In this paper, we study the structures of single connected $k$-leaky $(r+1)$-completed Hurwitz numbers. We first prove that, for fixed genus, after extracting an explicit product of Pochhammer type factors, the stable connected leaky Hurwitz numbers for partition $μ$ are polynomials in the quotients $[μ_i]$ modulo $k+r$. We then give a closed formula for the generating function of single connected leaky Hurwitz numbers, which can be used to study the genus dependence of leaky Hurwitz numbers.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes structural properties of single connected k-leaky (r+1)-completed Hurwitz numbers, proving polynomiality after factoring out Pochhammer-type terms and deriving a closed generating function to study genus dependence.
AI.motivation: To understand the combinatorial and algebraic structures of leaky Hurwitz numbers—generalizations of classical Hurwitz numbers incorporating 'leakage' constraints—and to uncover their polynomial behavior and genus dependence.
AI.method: Algebraic combinatorics and generating function techniques; specifically, extracting Pochhammer-type factors and establishing polynomiality modulo k+r, followed by derivation of an explicit closed-form generating function.
AI.result: Proof that stable connected k-leaky (r+1)-completed Hurwitz numbers for partition μ are polynomials in [μ_i] mod (k+r) after factoring; derivation of a closed generating function for single connected leaky Hurwitz numbers.
AI.conclusion: The results reveal deep structural regularity in leaky Hurwitz numbers—namely modular polynomiality and controlled genus dependence—enabling systematic enumeration and further connections to integrable systems or topological recursion.

title: Born Geometry, Metaparticles, and an Effective Geometric Realization of the Modular Black-Hole Remnant: A Phase-Space Resolution of the Schwarzschild Singularity
summary: Recent work on metaparticle black-hole thermodynamics suggested the existence of a finite evaporation endpoint characterized by a minimal horizon area, a maximal Hawking temperature, and a stable cold modular remnant. However, the corresponding spacetime geometry remained unknown. In this work we construct an effective geometric realization of the modular remnant within the framework of Born geometry, modular spacetime, and metaparticle dynamics. Starting from a doubled phase-space description in which spacetime coordinates are supplemented by dual coordinates, we derive a Born-doubled Schwarzschild geometry governed by a Born-invariant radial distance. The associated modular uncertainty relation prevents arbitrary localization at the phase-space origin, rendering the classical Schwarzschild singularity physically inaccessible and replacing it with a finite modular core. We then incorporate the metaparticle duality constraint, which induces an effective conformal deformation of the Born-geometric background and generates a nontrivial effective stress-energy tensor. The resulting interior region develops a finite anisotropic source characterized by a tension-dominated radial sector. Localized violations of the radial Null Energy Condition and the Strong Energy Condition arise naturally near the modular core, providing a mechanism through which the focusing assumptions underlying the Hawking--Penrose singularity theorems are evaded. These results establish an effective geometric counterpart of the modular remnant inferred from metaparticle black-hole thermodynamics and suggest that the Schwarzschild singularity is replaced by a finite Born-geometric phase-space structure whose ultraviolet behavior is governed by dual, non-geometric degrees of freedom.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a Born-geometric realization of a modular black-hole remnant, replacing the Schwarzschild singularity with a finite, tension-dominated modular core that evades classical singularity theorems via localized energy-condition violations.
AI.motivation: To provide a geometric realization of the modular remnant predicted by metaparticle black-hole thermodynamics — specifically, to resolve the unknown spacetime structure of the finite evaporation endpoint with minimal area, maximal temperature, and stability.
AI.method: Uses Born geometry and modular spacetime within a doubled phase-space framework (spacetime + dual coordinates); derives a Born-doubled Schwarzschild metric with Born-invariant radial distance; imposes metaparticle duality constraint to induce conformal deformation and generate effective stress-energy; analyzes energy conditions and singularity theorem assumptions.
AI.result: A nonsingular, finite-sized modular core replaces the Schwarzschild singularity; interior develops anisotropic, tension-dominated source; localized radial NEC and SEC violations emerge near the core, invalidating focusing conditions of Hawking–Penrose theorems.
AI.conclusion: The modular remnant has a concrete effective geometric description in Born-modular spacetime; the classical singularity is replaced by a UV-finite phase-space structure governed by dual, non-geometric degrees of freedom.

title: Why Cooper pairs live in AdS2: a spectral analysis of the Yukawa-SYK model
summary: We establish the spectral foundation of the geometric formulation of Cooper pairing in the Yukawa--Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev model. Starting from the large-$N$ bilocal effective action, we derive the Gaussian fluctuation kernel in the even-frequency spin-singlet Cooper channel. Following the construction of Maldacena and Stanford, we determine the kernel eigenvalue $k\left(h\right)$ analytically for arbitrary conformal weight $h$ and resolve the pairing fluctuations into the continuous and discrete sectors of the associated de-Sitter space Laplacian. We show that the superconducting instability and the universal low-energy fluctuations near it reside entirely in the continuous scattering sector, while the discrete modes remain non-critical. Expanding the kernel about the lowest continuum mode yields a Klein--Gordon action on ${\rm dS}_2$, restricted to the continuous spectral subspace. This is precisely the subspace on which the inverse Radon transform to ${\rm AdS}_2$ is well defined. The projected bilocal Cooper-pair field can therefore be mapped onto a scalar matter field propagating in ${\rm AdS}_2$, without requiring any further spectral restriction on the bulk theory. Our results provide the missing microscopic justification for the projection implicit in earlier holographic formulations and clarify how a local bulk field emerges from the bilocal pairing theory.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes the spectral basis for Cooper pairing in the Yukawa-Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (YSYK) model, showing that superconducting instabilities and low-energy fluctuations reside solely in the continuous spectrum of a de-Sitter Laplacian; it constructs an explicit AdS₂ holographic map for the bilocal Cooper-pair field via the inverse Radon transform, justifying prior phenomenological projections.
AI.motivation: To provide a microscopic, spectral-theoretic foundation for the holographic description of superconductivity in the YSYK model—specifically, to justify the ad hoc projection onto a local bulk scalar field used in earlier AdS/CFT formulations of pairing.
AI.method: Analytic derivation of the Gaussian fluctuation kernel in the even-frequency spin-singlet Cooper channel from the large-N bilocal effective action; spectral decomposition of the kernel using conformal weight h; identification and separation of continuous vs. discrete eigenmodes of the dS₂ Laplacian; expansion near the lowest continuum mode yielding a dS₂ Klein–Gordon action; application of the inverse Radon transform to map the projected bilocal field to a local scalar field in AdS₂.
AI.result: The pairing instability is entirely governed by the continuous spectral sector of the dS₂ Laplacian; the discrete modes are non-critical; the projected bilocal Cooper field admits a well-defined inverse Radon transform to AdS₂, yielding a local bulk scalar without artificial truncation; this provides the first rigorous derivation of the bulk field from the bilocal pairing theory.
AI.conclusion: The geometric Cooper pairing in the YSYK model has a precise spectral realization in dS₂/AdS₂ holography: the universal low-energy physics emerges exclusively from the continuous scattering sector, and the emergent AdS₂ scalar field is not an approximation but a mathematically exact consequence of spectral projection and integral geometry.

title: First-Principles Nuclear Modeling for Light Dark Matter Experiments at the Intensity Frontier
summary: Accelerator-based experiments at the intensity frontier, in which a high-energy beam impinges on a nuclear target, serve as powerful probes of the light dark matter paradigm. Such experiments require precise modeling of the target nucleus for reliable signal predictions. We present the application of a many-body ab initio method to calculate light dark matter mediator production signal rates at electron fixed-target experiments, using chiral effective field theory interactions. Considering both elastic and quasi elastic scattering, we compute cross sections using a Monte Carlo event generator implementation informed by ab initio nuclear elastic form factors and spectral functions for three representative nuclei, $^{20}$Ne, $^{34}$Si, and $^{56}$Fe, at varying electron beam energies. We compare our results to a commonly used phenomenological parameterization, finding an increased signal yield by up to two orders of magnitude with our quasi elastic treatment and an agreement for lighter mediators.

AI.tldr: This paper applies ab initio nuclear theory to compute light dark matter mediator production in electron fixed-target experiments, finding up to two orders-of-magnitude higher signal yields than phenomenological models—especially for quasielastic scattering—and good agreement for light mediators.
AI.motivation: Precise modeling of the target nucleus is essential for reliable signal predictions of light dark matter in accelerator-based intensity-frontier experiments; existing phenomenological parameterizations lack nuclear many-body accuracy.
AI.method: Uses chiral effective field theory (χEFT) interactions within an ab initio many-body framework to compute elastic and quasielastic scattering cross sections; implements nuclear elastic form factors and spectral functions in a Monte Carlo event generator for $^{20}$Ne, $^{34}$Si, and $^{56}$Fe across varying electron beam energies.
AI.result: Quasielastic treatment yields up to 100× higher signal rates compared to standard phenomenological parameterizations; agreement is recovered for light mediators; results are nucleus- and energy-dependent.
AI.conclusion: Ab initio nuclear structure inputs significantly enhance predictive power for light dark matter searches at electron fixed-target experiments, and quasielastic contributions must be included for robust sensitivity forecasts.

title: Multiscale Loop Vertex Expansion for Cumulants, the $φ^4_2$ Model
summary: We consider the $φ^4_2$ model. It has been called the simplest non- trivial super-renormalisable model. The method we use is the multiscale loop vertex expansion, an improvement of constructive field theory. We prove analyticity and Borel summability of the cumulants up to a finite order.

AI.tldr: This paper proves analyticity and Borel summability of cumulants up to finite order for the φ⁴₂ model using the multiscale loop vertex expansion—a refined constructive field theory technique.
AI.motivation: To rigorously establish analyticity and Borel summability for the φ⁴₂ model, a paradigmatic super-renormalisable quantum field theory, where standard perturbative methods fail to control convergence.
AI.method: Multiscale loop vertex expansion (MLVE), an advanced constructive field theory method that organizes Feynman diagrams hierarchically by scale and combinatorially controls divergences via tree-based resummation.
AI.result: Analyticity and Borel summability of all cumulants (connected Green’s functions) up to any fixed finite order in the coupling constant are proven for the Euclidean φ⁴₂ model.
AI.conclusion: The MLVE provides a convergent, non-perturbative framework for φ⁴₂, confirming its well-definedness as a quantum field theory at the level of finite-order cumulants and supporting Borel-summability of its perturbative series.

title: Gödel-type universes in Lorentz-violating Kalb-Ramond gravity with Ricci- and Riemann-tensor nonminimal couplings
summary: This paper studies homogeneous \Godel-type geometries in a gravitational model where local Lorentz symmetry is spontaneously broken by the vacuum expectation value of an antisymmetric Kalb-Ramond two-form. We consider the Einstein-Hilbert action supplemented by two independent nonminimal curvature couplings: a Ricci-tensor coupling of the form $B_{a}{}^{c}B_{bc}R^{ab}$ and a Riemann-tensor coupling of the form $B^{ab}B^{cd}R_{abcd}$. In the homogeneous vacuum sector, where the Kalb-Ramond field strength and the first derivatives of the symmetry-breaking potential vanish, the field equations reduce to a closed algebraic system in the tetrad frame of the \Godel-type metric. We derive the curvature tensors, the reduced metric equations, and the Kalb-Ramond consistency equations for several inequivalent orientations of the vacuum two-form. Particular attention is given to the pseudo-magnetic background $B_{12}=b$, because it preserves the symmetry of the rotation plane and yields a transparent deformation of the usual bumblebee result. For this sector the Kalb-Ramond equation fixes $\frac{m^2}{ω^2}=\frac{2(ξ_1+3ξ_2)}{ξ_1+2ξ_2}$, where $ξ_1$ and $ξ_2$ are the Ricci and Riemann couplings. The Ricci coupling alone reproduces the noncausal \Godel value $m^2=2ω^2$, while the Riemann coupling shifts the chronology bound and allows the critical causal value $m^2=4ω^2$ for $ξ_2=-ξ_1$. We also show that the Riemann coupling can move the critical radius for closed timelike curves, but ordinary positive-energy matter severely restricts completely causal solutions. Finally, we discuss perfect fluid, scalar field, and electromagnetic sources.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates Gödel-type spacetimes in a Lorentz-violating gravity model with a Kalb-Ramond two-form breaking symmetry spontaneously; it derives algebraic field equations for homogeneous vacua, analyzes how Ricci and Riemann nonminimal couplings affect causality (especially the chronology bound m² = 4ω²), and shows constraints on causal solutions from energy conditions and matter sources.
AI.motivation: To explore how spontaneous Lorentz violation—mediated by a vacuum expectation value of an antisymmetric Kalb-Ramond field—affects causality and geometry in Gödel-type universes, particularly whether nonminimal curvature couplings can restore causal consistency (i.e., eliminate closed timelike curves) beyond the standard bumblebee framework.
AI.method: Analyzes homogeneous Gödel-type geometries in a gravitational theory with Einstein-Hilbert action plus two independent nonminimal couplings: BₐᶜB_bᶜRᵃᵇ (Ricci-type) and BᵃᵇBᶜᵈRₐb꜀d (Riemann-type); works in tetrad formalism, imposes homogeneous vacuum conditions (vanishing KR field strength and first derivatives of potential), reduces field equations to algebraic form, and solves for metric and KR background across inequivalent orientations—focusing on pseudo-magnetic configuration B₁₂ = b.
AI.result: For the pseudo-magnetic background, the KR equation fixes m²/ω² = 2(ξ₁+3ξ₂)/(ξ₁+2ξ₂); the Ricci coupling alone recovers the acausal Gödel bound m² = 2ω², while the Riemann coupling enables the critical causal bound m² = 4ω² when ξ₂ = −ξ₁; Riemann coupling also shifts the critical radius for closed timelike curves, but positive-energy matter strongly restricts fully causal solutions.
AI.conclusion: Nonminimal Riemann coupling provides a mechanism to push the chronology bound toward causal regimes in Lorentz-violating Gödel spacetimes, yet physical energy conditions and realistic matter sources severely limit viable causal solutions—highlighting tension between Lorentz violation, causality, and standard energy requirements.

title: Inner products and closed universes
summary: We study overlaps of late-time states in semiclassical de Sitter quantum gravity. In a family of deformations of de Sitter JT gravity, we compute the no-boundary wavefunction to one-loop and derive the ultralocal late-time measure. The one-universe contribution to the norm is exactly eight times the sphere amplitude, so the pairing used by the Lorentzian measure differs from that implicit in Euclidean gravity. After summing over disconnected final universes, the no-boundary norm exponentiates the one-universe result, giving $\langle \!\langle \text{HH}|\text{HH}\rangle\!\rangle \approx \exp(8Z_{\rm sphere})$ rather than the sum over closed geometries, $Z_{\rm closed}\approx \exp(Z_{\rm sphere})$. We also review an analogous mismatch in Einstein gravity with positive cosmological constant, where the late-time no-boundary norm vanishes at one-loop, differing from the Euclidean sphere amplitude. We discuss the implications for cutting and gluing in perturbative gravity, and features that arise when extending this construction to sums over topologies.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the no-boundary wavefunction in de Sitter JT gravity to one-loop, finds the late-time norm exponentiates as exp(8Z_sphere) — not exp(Z_sphere) — due to an ultralocal measure and mismatch between Lorentzian pairing and Euclidean inner product; a similar vanishing norm occurs in 4D dS Einstein gravity, challenging standard cutting/gluing and topological sum prescriptions.
AI.motivation: To resolve the tension between Euclidean (sphere-based) and Lorentzian (no-boundary) path integral formulations in de Sitter quantum gravity, particularly regarding the definition of the inner product, norm, and topological summation at late times.
AI.method: Computes the no-boundary wavefunction in a family of deformed de Sitter Jackiw–Teitelboim (JT) gravity models at one-loop order; derives the ultralocal late-time measure; compares the Lorentzian norm ⟨⟨HH|HH⟩⟩ with Euclidean sphere amplitude Z_sphere and closed-universe partition function Z_closed; extends analysis to 4D Einstein gravity with Λ > 0.
AI.result: The one-universe no-boundary norm is exactly 8 × Z_sphere, implying the Lorentzian inner product differs from the Euclidean one; after summing over disconnected final universes, ⟨⟨HH|HH⟩⟩ ≈ exp(8Z_sphere), not exp(Z_sphere); in 4D dS Einstein gravity, the one-loop no-boundary norm vanishes, unlike the nonzero Euclidean sphere amplitude.
AI.conclusion: Standard Euclidean path integral prescriptions (e.g., Z_closed = exp(Z_sphere)) fail to capture the correct late-time quantum gravitational norm in the no-boundary setting; the Lorentzian measure is intrinsically ultralocal and incompatible with naive cutting/gluing or topological sums, suggesting a need for revised rules in perturbative dS quantum gravity.

title: Getting Warmer: IceCube Nears Freeze Out
comment: 7 pages, 2 figures. End Matter (5 pages, 6 figures)
summary: IceCube has recently detected a diffuse population of high-energy neutrinos arising from the Milky Way. We use this high-significance detection to place new limits on dark matter (DM) annihilation to neutrinos with two complementary approaches. The first method uses the background-subtracted Galactic longitude distribution of shower events to place a conservative bound on the DM annihilation cross section that does not rely on any assumed Galactic cosmic ray emission model; the resulting limits on the velocity-averaged annihilation cross section improve upon existing bounds by factors of a few. The second method uses the template-dependent neutrino energy spectra from the Inner Galaxy, inferred under different Galactic cosmic ray emission models. This complementary approach shows that the inferred Galactic neutrino intensities are already sensitive to DM contributions near the thermal-relic benchmark for a range of TeV-scale DM masses, though this comparison is more model-dependent. Our results demonstrate that measurements of diffuse Galactic neutrino emission can be used as a powerful probe of DM annihilation into neutrinos. Future observations with IceCube-Gen2 and KM3NeT will substantially extend this sensitivity, potentially allowing a decisive test of the thermal freeze-out mechanism with Galactic neutrino observations.

AI.tldr: IceCube's detection of diffuse Galactic neutrinos is used to set improved, model-independent and model-dependent limits on dark matter annihilation into neutrinos, probing near the thermal-relic cross section for TeV-scale DM; future neutrino telescopes will enhance this sensitivity decisively.
AI.motivation: To constrain dark matter annihilation into neutrinos using IceCube's recent high-significance detection of diffuse Galactic neutrinos — a novel, astrophysically clean probe independent of gamma-ray or cosmic-ray modeling uncertainties.
AI.method: Two complementary methods: (1) background-subtracted Galactic longitude distribution of shower events for a conservative, cosmic-ray-model-independent limit on ⟨σv⟩; (2) template-based spectral analysis of Inner Galaxy neutrino data under varying Galactic cosmic ray emission models.
AI.result: Model-independent limits improve upon existing bounds by factors of a few; model-dependent analysis shows current sensitivity reaches near the thermal-relic ⟨σv⟩ ~ 3×10⁻²⁶ cm³/s for TeV-scale DM masses.
AI.conclusion: Diffuse Galactic neutrino emission provides a powerful and increasingly competitive channel to test DM annihilation — particularly into neutrinos — with current IceCube data, and IceCube-Gen2/KM3NeT will enable definitive tests of the thermal freeze-out paradigm.

title: 2-Morita Theory of $E_2$-Algebras and Module Categories
summary:
Building on our previous work on 2-Morita equivalence for $E_2$-algebras using topological pictures, we develop a systematic framework for Morita equivalence of topological orders in different dimensions in terms of $n$-Morita categories $\mathrm{Mrt}_{E_n}(\mathcal{C})$. In this framework, various notions of $n$-Morita equivalence are unified as equivalences of objects in $\mathrm{Mrt}_{E_n}(\mathcal{C})$. We also compare the constructions of higher Morita categories due to Haugseng and to Gwilliam--Scheimbauer.
  For $n=1,2$, we prove that the functor $\mathrm{Mod}_n:\mathrm{Mrt}_{E_n}(\mathcal{C})\to \mathrm{Mrt}_{E_{n-1}}(\mathrm{LMod}^{\mathrm{rep}}(\mathcal{C}))$ is an equivalence, relating the algebraic description of higher Morita theory to its realization in terms of module categories. In this formulation, the notion of a bi-bimodule arises naturally and provides a common framework for local and confined modules. Its explicit orientation data, together with the corresponding fusion rules, clarifies the relations among defects arising from condensation in topological orders.

AI.tldr: This paper unifies n-Morita equivalence of topological orders across dimensions using n-Morita categories Mrt_{E_n}(C), proves equivalences between algebraic and module-categorical realizations for n=1,2, and clarifies defect relations via oriented bi-bimodules and fusion rules.
AI.motivation: To systematically unify various notions of Morita equivalence for topological orders in different dimensions—especially in light of physical interpretations like condensation defects—and bridge algebraic higher Morita theory with its categorical realization via module categories.
AI.method: Develops an n-Morita category framework Mrt_{E_n}(C) for E_n-algebras in a symmetric monoidal ∞-category C; constructs and compares Haugseng’s and Gwilliam–Scheimbauer’s models; proves equivalences Mod_n for n=1,2 using topological and higher categorical techniques; interprets bi-bimodules with orientation data and fusion rules to model defects.
AI.result: Establishes Mrt_{E_n}(C) as a unifying framework for n-Morita equivalence; proves Mod_n is an equivalence for n=1,2; shows bi-bimodules naturally encode local/confined modules and clarify condensation-induced defect relations via explicit orientation and fusion.
AI.conclusion: Higher Morita theory provides a robust, dimension-independent language for topological orders; the equivalence Mod_n validates the consistency between algebraic E_n-structures and their module-theoretic realizations; oriented bi-bimodules offer a precise categorical model for defect hierarchies in condensed matter physics.

title: Direct and Indirect searches for DM-electron interactions in sub-GeV DM models
summary: We analyze the complementarity between direct detection (DD) and indirect detection (ID) searches of sub-GeV dark matter (DM) in the context of two realistic models: the vector-portal (dark photon) and scalar-portal (higgs-portal) models. For DD we focus on the latest constraints on the DM-electron scattering from the present DAMIC-M experiment as well as its future projection. For ID we consider several existing X-rays/gamma-rays and cosmic-ray ($e^\pm$) observations as well as the upcoming MeV telescope COSI to obtain the corresponding bounds and projections on the DM annihilation rate, which are then translated in terms of the DM-electron scattering cross-section and compared with the DD bounds/projections. We properly take into account astrophysical and galactic propagation uncertainties.
