We find that the complementarity between DAMIC-M and ID works best for the vector-portal model, especially for the case where the vector mediator is heavier than the DM particle: in this case, the present DAMIC-M bound becomes comparable to (or better than, for some astrophysical configurations) the combined ID limit for $3\,{\rm MeV} \lesssim m_{\rm DM} \lesssim 20\,{\rm MeV}$. For other cases and mass ranges, the ID is in general more constraining and can also, for some mass ranges, constrain the parameter space below the neutrino floor, which is inaccessible to DD experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the complementarity between direct detection (DD) and indirect detection (ID) for sub-GeV dark matter in vector- and scalar-portal models, comparing DAMIC-M (DD) constraints/projections with X-ray/gamma-ray/cosmic-ray (ID) bounds—including COSI—while accounting for astrophysical uncertainties; it finds DD and ID are most complementary in the heavy-vector-mediator regime of the dark photon model (3–20 MeV DM), whereas ID dominates elsewhere and can probe below the neutrino floor.
AI.motivation: To assess how direct and indirect detection strategies jointly constrain sub-GeV dark matter parameter space—particularly where traditional DD faces sensitivity limits (e.g., neutrino floor)—and to quantify the role of astrophysical uncertainties and experimental projections in realistic portal models.
AI.method: Combined analysis of current and projected DD limits from DAMIC-M (DM-electron scattering) with ID constraints from X-ray/gamma-ray (e.g., INTEGRAL, Fermi-LAT) and cosmic-ray (e.g., AMS-02) data, plus future COSI sensitivity; translation of ID annihilation rate bounds into equivalent DM-electron scattering cross-sections; inclusion of galactic propagation and astrophysical uncertainties (e.g., DM density profile, electron energy losses, background modeling).
AI.result: For the vector-portal model with mediator mass > DM mass, DAMIC-M’s present bound rivals or exceeds combined ID limits for 3–20 MeV DM depending on astrophysical assumptions; for scalar-portal and lighter/heavier DM or light-mediator vector cases, ID provides stronger constraints—and in some ranges probes below the neutrino floor, inaccessible to DD.
AI.conclusion: DD and ID are highly complementary for sub-GeV DM, especially in the heavy-dark-photon regime; full exploitation requires joint analysis incorporating propagation and astrophysical systematics, and future experiments like COSI will significantly extend ID reach beyond DD limitations.

title: Comparison of Two-Atom Cross Spectra in de Sitter Spacetime, Uniformly Accelerated Minkowski Vacuum, and a Thermal Bath
summary: We study the weak coupling of two identical two-level atoms to a four-dimensional massless conformally coupled scalar field and compare three settings with the same local temperature but different physical origins: comoving atoms in the Bunch--Davies vacuum of de Sitter spacetime, transversely separated uniformly accelerated atoms in the Minkowski vacuum, and static atoms in a Minkowski thermal bath. We first derive the two-atom cross spectra in the three settings and then obtain the single-atom local spectra uniformly from the zero-separation limit. When $a=H$ and $β=2π/H$, the complete local Wightman kernels and local spectra are identical in all three cases. At finite separation, a genuine thermal bath produces a $\sinc(ΩL)$ spatial factor, whereas de Sitter spacetime and the transversely accelerated vacuum produce a hyperbolic geometric factor. In the long-distance limit, the cross correlations in de Sitter spacetime and the transversely accelerated vacuum decay as $L^{-2}$, whereas those in the Minkowski thermal bath decay only as $L^{-1}$. The de Sitter and transversely accelerated vacuum cross spectra coincide when $a=H$ and the separations are instantaneously matched. For a fixed experimental setup, the physical separation between the two comoving atoms in de Sitter space evolves with cosmic expansion, whereas the pulled-back cross correlations in the uniformly accelerated and thermal Minkowski configurations are stationary.

AI.tldr: This paper compares quantum correlations between two weakly coupled two-level atoms in three physically distinct but locally thermal settings—de Sitter (Bunch–Davies vacuum), transversely uniformly accelerated atoms in Minkowski vacuum, and static atoms in a Minkowski thermal bath—finding identical local spectra when local temperature matches (a = H, β = 2π/H), but qualitatively different nonlocal (cross) spectral structures due to underlying geometry vs. true thermality.
AI.motivation: To distinguish genuine thermal effects from geometric (vacuum) effects that mimic local thermality—specifically, whether local temperature alone determines quantum correlations or whether global spacetime structure (e.g., curvature or acceleration horizon) leaves imprints on nonlocal observables like two-atom cross spectra.
AI.method: Computes the two-atom symmetric (Wightman-based) cross spectra and local spectra from the zero-separation limit, using perturbative weak-coupling formalism within quantum field theory in curved spacetime; analytically compares functional forms of spatial correlation factors (sinc vs. hyperbolic) and asymptotic decay laws (L⁻¹ vs. L⁻²) across the three settings.
AI.result: Local spectra coincide exactly when a = H and β = 2π/H; however, cross spectra differ: thermal bath yields sinc(ΩL), while de Sitter and transverse acceleration yield hyperbolic spatial factors; long-distance decay is L⁻¹ for thermal bath vs. L⁻² for the other two; de Sitter and accelerated cases agree only when instantaneous separations match and a = H; comoving separation evolves cosmologically, whereas Minkowski configurations are stationary.
AI.conclusion: Local temperature is insufficient to fully characterize interatomic quantum correlations; global causal structure and geometry imprint distinct signatures on nonlocal observables, enabling experimental discrimination between true thermal baths and effective thermality arising from acceleration or cosmic expansion.

title: Contact Structure-induced Symplectic Nearly Half-Flat $SU(3)$ Structure in Finite-$N$ Thermal ${\cal M}$-Theory
summary: The ${\cal M}$-theory dual of thermal QCD-like theories constructed in arXiv:1306.4339, 2004.07259 involves, as shown in arXiv:2211.13186, a closed $G_2$-structure seven-fold $\mathcal{M}_7$ supporting Contact 3-Structures (C3S) that induce a ``transverse'' $SU(3)$-structure. We prove that this induced structure belongs to the symplectic nearly half-flat (S(nearly)HF) class: $dω_Φ=0$ exactly, while $dΩ_+$ is suppressed as $\mathcal{O}(e^{-N^{1/3}/\mathcal{O}(1)})$ in the infrared "MQGP limit", leaving $W_Φ^{SU(3)}=W_2^-$ as the sole non-vanishing Chiossi--Salamon torsion class and completing the $G$-structure classification of the MQGP dual initiated in arXiv:1507.02692,2004.07259, 2211.13186. As a physical application, Kaluza--Klein reduction of the eleven-dimensional Hodge dual of the differential of the $G_2$-structure positive three-form on $\mathcal{M}_7$, organised through the $G_2$/S(nearly)HF torsion data, yields a radial ``magnetic field'' $\mathcal{B}_{\rm KK}(r)$ whose squared norm factorises exactly into external and internal factors. $\mathcal{B}_{\rm KK}(r)$ satisfies a Bessel-type ODE with a regular singular point at the horizon; normalisability and infrared regularity select $J_2$, with harmonicity of the aforementioned internal factor recovered from the large-$N$ suppression. $\mathcal{B}_{\rm KK}$ is related to the magnetic field of the type~IIA flavour $D6$-branes via a non-linear power law, furnishing a top-down holographic mechanism for generating weak magnetic fields in finite-temperature string theory.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes that the induced SU(3)-structure on the seven-fold M₇ dual to thermal QCD-like theories belongs to the symplectic nearly half-flat (S(nearly)HF) class, with exact dω_Φ = 0 and exponentially suppressed dΩ₊ in the MQGP limit; it then uses this classification to perform a Kaluza–Klein reduction yielding a radial magnetic field B_KK(r) satisfying a Bessel-type ODE, whose infrared behavior and relation to D6-brane magnetism provide a top-down holographic mechanism for weak magnetic fields in finite-temperature string theory.
AI.motivation: To complete the G-structure classification of the M-theory dual of thermal QCD-like theories (the MQGP background) and to derive physical consequences—specifically, a holographically generated weak magnetic field—via torsion-based Kaluza–Klein reduction.
AI.method: Rigorous analysis of the induced transverse SU(3)-structure on the closed G₂-manifold M₇ using Chiossi–Salamon torsion classes; application of the MQGP limit to quantify suppression of torsion components; Kaluza–Klein reduction of the Hodge dual of dφ (where φ is the G₂-positive 3-form), organized by S(nearly)HF torsion data; analysis of the resulting radial 'magnetic' field via ODE theory (Bessel equation, regular singular point, normalizability, large-N asymptotics).
AI.result: The induced SU(3)-structure is proven to be symplectic nearly half-flat: dω_Φ ≡ 0 and dΩ₊ = O(e^{−N^{1/3}/O(1)}), leaving only W₂⁻ non-vanishing; the KK-reduced field B_KK(r) factorises exactly, satisfies a J₂-Bessel ODE, and is related to D6-brane magnetism via a non-linear power law.
AI.conclusion: The MQGP dual’s geometric structure is fully classified within the S(nearly)HF class, enabling a consistent, top-down holographic derivation of weak magnetic fields in finite-temperature string theory—linking internal G-structure torsion, IR dynamics, and observable gauge-field phenomena.

title: Enhancement of nonlinear pair production in a flying-focus pulse
summary: A photon can decay into an electron-positron pair in the presence of an intense laser pulse by a process known as nonlinear Breit-Wheeler pair production (NBWPP). For a sufficiently intense pulse, the probability of NBWPP for a high-energy gamma photon scales more favorably with the interaction time than with the field intensity. In contrast to typical stationary-focus Gaussian (SFG) laser pulses, a flying-focus (FF) pulse features a focal point that moves at a programmable velocity. Here, we show that a FF pulse counterpropagating with a high-energy photon beam while its focus copropagates with the beam at the speed of light enhances the NBWPP yield relative to an equal-energy SFG pulse. Numerical simulations show that a Joule-class tightly-focused FF pulse allows for an enhancement of the pair-production yield by 12\%, 29\% and 76\% for a photon of 10, 20 and 50 GeV energy, respectively. Thus, in this regime, FF pulses are more efficient at producing electron-positron pairs than conventional SFG pulses.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that flying-focus (FF) laser pulses—whose focal point moves at programmable velocity—enhance nonlinear Breit-Wheeler pair production (NBWPP) when counterpropagating with high-energy gamma photons, outperforming stationary-focus Gaussian (SFG) pulses by up to 76% for 50 GeV photons.
AI.motivation: To improve the efficiency of electron-positron pair production via nonlinear Breit-Wheeler process using intense lasers, especially where interaction time scaling dominates over field intensity scaling.
AI.method: Numerical simulations comparing NBWPP yields from counterpropagating high-energy gamma photons interacting with Joule-class tightly-focused flying-focus (FF) pulses versus equal-energy stationary-focus Gaussian (SFG) pulses; FF pulse configured so its focus copropagates with photons at c while the pulse itself counterpropagates.
AI.result: FF pulses yield 12%, 29%, and 76% higher pair-production for 10, 20, and 50 GeV photons respectively, relative to SFG pulses of equal energy.
AI.conclusion: Flying-focus laser pulses are more efficient than conventional SFG pulses for NBWPP in the regime where interaction time governs scaling, enabling enhanced laboratory-scale QED pair production.

title: Casimir operators of $4D\,, \mathcal{N}=2$ supersymmetry in the harmonic approach

Specifically, the superisospin operator $C_I$ is expressed in terms of new 'long' harmonic derivatives $

We also construct $\mathcal{N}=2$ superhelicity and super-isohelicity operators relevant to the massless case (with vanishing $\Box$) and find their eigenvalues for few instructive examples of $4D, \,\mathcal{N}=2$ superfield theories.

AI.motivation: To systematically construct and characterize Casimir operators of the 4D, N=2 supersymmetry algebra within the harmonic superspace framework—particularly to accommodate analytic superfields and enable classification of irreducible representations, including massless ones.
AI.method: Uses harmonic superspace formalism with analytic basis; introduces non-local 'long' harmonic derivatives ∇^{±±}, ∇^0 involving □^{-1}; derives Casimir operators—including superisospin C_I—by expressing them covariantly in terms of these derivatives; constructs superhelicity and super-isohelicity operators for the massless (□ = 0) sector and evaluates their eigenvalues on selected superfield models.
AI.result: Explicit expression for the superisospin Casimir C_I = (1/4)(∇^0)^2 + (1/2){∇^{++}, ∇^{--}}; derivation of modified SU(2) commutation relations where ∇^0 eigenvalues are shifted by −2 relative to standard U(1) charges; construction of superhelicity and super-isohelicity operators; explicit eigenvalues computed for representative N=2 superfield theories (e.g., hypermultiplet, vector multiplet).
AI.conclusion: The non-local harmonic derivative framework consistently realizes the full N=2 supersymmetry Casimirs, enabling a refined representation-theoretic analysis—especially for massless multiplets—and reveals structural deviations from standard harmonic algebra due to analyticity constraints.

title: $μ$DM: a new mechanism for the baryon-dark matter coincidence
summary: For a relativistically decoupled thermal relic, the dark-matter energy-to-entropy ratio scales as $ρ_{\rm DM}/s\sim 10^{-3}m_{\rm DM}$. This is the familiar hot-dark-matter abundance relation. Immediately after weak-sphaleron freeze-out, the baryon asymmetry can be parametrized as $ρ_{\rm baryon}/s\sim 10^{-4}|μ_B|$. Here $μ_B$ is the baryon-number chemical potential. We propose a new class of models, called chemical-potential-matched dark matter ($μ$DM), in which $|μ_B|\sim m_{\rm DM}$, thereby providing a new route to the baryon-dark matter coincidence. As a concrete example of $μ$DM, we consider an Affleck-Dine field whose excitations constitute dark matter. We also briefly discuss spontaneous electroweak baryogenesis associated with axion-like-particle walls. In the absence of entropy dilution, this coincidence mechanism generically points to dark matter in the eV-keV mass range. Its momentum distribution can nevertheless be cold if thermal production is dominated by Bose-enhanced stimulated emission. Alternatively, entropy dilution after both the dark-matter and baryon yields are fixed allows masses up to the MeV scale.

AI.tldr: Proposes a new 'chemical-potential-matched dark matter' (μDM) framework linking baryon asymmetry and dark matter abundance via equality of baryon chemical potential |μ_B| and DM mass m_DM, naturally explaining their cosmic coincidence; concrete realizations include Affleck-Dine DM and axion-like-particle wall baryogenesis; predicts DM mass in eV–keV (cold if Bose-enhanced) or up to MeV with entropy dilution.
AI.motivation: To explain the observed cosmic coincidence ρ_DM / ρ_baryon ≈ 5 without fine-tuning, by relating the dark matter abundance and baryon asymmetry through a common physical scale—the baryon-number chemical potential μ_B—rather than independent freeze-out dynamics.
AI.method: Analyzes thermal relic scaling relations for relativistically decoupled DM and baryons post weak-sphaleron freeze-out; introduces μDM paradigm where |μ_B| ∼ m_DM; constructs explicit models: (i) Affleck-Dine field excitations as DM, (ii) spontaneous EW baryogenesis on axion-like-particle domain walls; incorporates Bose enhancement and entropy dilution to reconcile light mass with cold kinematics.
AI.result: μDM yields ρ_DM/s ∼ ρ_baryon/s when |μ_B| ∼ m_DM, explaining the abundance ratio; predicts DM mass m_DM ∼ eV–keV without entropy dilution (cold due to stimulated emission), or up to MeV if entropy dilution occurs after both yields are fixed.
AI.conclusion: The μDM mechanism provides a theoretically motivated, non-fine-tuned explanation for the baryon–dark matter coincidence, with testable implications for DM mass, production mechanism, and phase-space distribution—distinguishing it from standard thermal WIMP or sterile neutrino scenarios.

title: Relativistic Modeling for Solid Earth Tide Estimation via Space-to-Ground Clock Comparison
summary: With the rapid development of modern atomic clock technology, their unprecedented precision elevates them from timekeeping tools to gravitational potential sensors, thereby fostering the highly interdisciplinary field of Relativistic Geodesy. Given the potential for high-precision clock networks to detect periodic gravitational variations, it is imperative to assess their capability to invert solid Earth tide parameters via space-to-ground links in the presence of complex observational noise. To this end, we incorporate Earth's gravitational potential, direct lunisolar tidal potentials, and solid Earth tide effects into a high-precision relativistic framework for space-to-ground clock comparisons. By employing a three-link Doppler cancellation configuration to isolate the target signal, we perform numerical simulations for an inclined geosynchronous orbit satellite to analyze the effects of clock instability and colored precise orbit determination errors on parameter extraction. Our findings reveal that while high orbital altitudes cause severe collinearity between individual Love numbers, an effective parameter combining the $h_2$ and $k_2$ Love numbers successfully converges to a stable estimate within a 30-day continuous observation window. Furthermore, sensitivity analysis demonstrates that extraction accuracy is currently limited by clock stability rather than radial precise orbit determination errors.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates using high-precision atomic clocks in space-to-ground links for relativistic geodesy, specifically to invert solid Earth tide parameters (e.g., Love numbers h₂, k₂) amid noise; it finds that a combined h₂–k₂ parameter is estimable within 30 days, and clock instability—not orbit errors—is the current limiting factor.
AI.motivation: To assess the capability of high-precision clock networks to invert solid Earth tide parameters (especially Love numbers) via space-to-ground relativistic frequency comparisons, given their emerging role as gravitational potential sensors in relativistic geodesy.
AI.method: Develops a high-precision relativistic model incorporating Earth’s gravitational potential, direct lunisolar tidal potentials, and solid Earth tide effects; uses a three-link Doppler cancellation scheme to isolate tidal signals; conducts numerical simulations with an inclined geosynchronous satellite under realistic clock instability and colored precise orbit determination (POD) errors.
AI.result: High orbital altitude induces strong collinearity between h₂ and k₂; however, a linear combination of h₂ and k₂ converges stably within 30 days of continuous observation; sensitivity analysis shows clock instability dominates estimation uncertainty, not radial POD errors.
AI.conclusion: Space-to-ground clock networks can constrain combined solid Earth tide parameters robustly over ~30 days, but further clock stability improvements are required to disentangle individual Love numbers—highlighting atomic clocks as the bottleneck, not orbit determination, in relativistic tidal geodesy.

title: Gravitational Compton Amplitude to All Orders in Perturbation Theory
summary: We show how amplitudes from the scattering of gravitational waves off compact objects in worldline effective field theory can be efficiently computed to arbitrary order in Newton's constant $G$. Our approach solves an effective wave equation for the partial-wave amplitude in which Wilson coefficients (tidal Love numbers) enter through boundary conditions at short distances. We then perform the sum over partial waves to obtain the momentum-space Compton amplitude in terms of elliptic polylogarithms. We reproduce recent results through $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ and obtain new predictions up to $\mathcal{O}(G^7)$, with Love numbers first contributing at $\mathcal{O}(G^5)$. We find the first ultraviolet divergence in a classical gravitational amplitude at $\mathcal{O}(G^7)$, showing that a pure point-particle description is not consistent in general relativity. Matching to black hole perturbation theory, we show that static Love numbers vanish on-shell and predict subleading non-zero Schwarzschild black hole Love numbers.

AI.tldr: This paper computes gravitational wave scattering amplitudes off compact objects using worldline EFT, solving an effective wave equation with tidal Love numbers as boundary conditions; it yields momentum-space Compton amplitudes in terms of elliptic polylogarithms, extends predictions to O(G⁷), reveals the first classical UV divergence at O(G⁷), and shows static Love numbers vanish for Schwarzschild black holes while predicting subleading non-zero ones.
AI.motivation: To systematically compute classical gravitational scattering amplitudes beyond point-particle approximations, resolve consistency of worldline EFT in general relativity, and clarify the role and values of tidal Love numbers for black holes.
AI.method: Solves an effective radial wave equation for partial-wave amplitudes in worldline effective field theory, incorporating tidal Wilson coefficients (Love numbers) via short-distance boundary conditions; performs partial-wave sum to obtain full momentum-space Compton amplitude expressed in elliptic polylogarithms.
AI.result: Reproduces known results up to O(G⁴); provides new analytical predictions up to O(G⁷); identifies first classical UV divergence at O(G⁷), signaling breakdown of pure point-particle description; confirms on-shell vanishing of static Love numbers for Schwarzschild black holes and predicts non-zero subleading (dynamical/curvature-coupled) Love numbers.
AI.conclusion: Worldline EFT with finite-size effects is essential for consistent classical GR amplitudes beyond O(G⁴); the O(G⁷) divergence necessitates UV completion or extended-object modeling; Schwarzschild black holes have no static tidal response but exhibit non-trivial higher-order tidal structure.

title: Proof of the AGT Conjecture at Generic $β$
summary: We give an all-level proof of the four-point $SU(2)$ AGT correspondence with four fundamental hypermultiplets at generic $β=-ε_1/ε_2$, by proving an all-level factorization formula for Selberg averages of generalized Jack polynomials. Taking a coefficientwise Jack limit of the generalized Macdonald Pieri rule, we obtain the required one-box matrix elements in the strict Cauchy dual basis. A rational corner-function identity then evaluates the sum over all parent double partitions, while an explicit total derivative of the Selberg kernel yields a triangular recursion on the Dotsenko-Fateev charge balance hyperplane. The unique solution of this recursion is the generalized Kadell formula previously verified only through finite level. Combining this result with the generalized Cauchy identity identifies each double partition term with the corresponding Nekrasov fixed-point contribution.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a complete, all-level proof of the four-point SU(2) AGT correspondence with four fundamental hypermultiplets at generic beta, by establishing a factorization formula for Selberg averages of generalized Jack polynomials via Pieri rules, corner-function identities, and a triangular recursion solved by the generalized Kadell formula.
AI.motivation: To rigorously prove the SU(2) AGT correspondence for the four-point function with four fundamental hypermultiplets at arbitrary beta, beyond previous finite-level verifications.
AI.method: Derives an all-level factorization formula for Selberg averages of generalized Jack polynomials using: (1) coefficientwise Jack limit of the generalized Macdonald Pieri rule to obtain one-box matrix elements in the strict Cauchy dual basis; (2) a rational corner-function identity to sum over parent double partitions; (3) explicit total derivative of the Selberg kernel to yield a triangular recursion on the Dotsenko-Fateev charge balance hyperplane.
AI.result: The unique solution of the triangular recursion is the generalized Kadell formula—previously confirmed only up to finite level—now established at all levels; combined with the generalized Cauchy identity, this identifies each double partition term with its corresponding Nekrasov fixed-point contribution.
AI.conclusion: The four-point SU(2) AGT correspondence with four fundamental hypermultiplets holds at generic beta to all orders, fully bridging Liouville conformal blocks and Nekrasov partition functions via exact combinatorial–analytic machinery.

title: Simulations and flavour-scheme studies for Higgs-boson production in association with charm quarks
comment: Contribution to the Report 5 collection of the LHC Higgs Working Group. Also available at the CERN Document Server: https://cds.cern.ch/record/2965814
summary: We present a detailed NLO+PS study of Higgs-boson production in association with charm and bottom quarks, with particular focus on the modelling of the H+c final state. We systematically compare predictions in massive and massless flavour schemes, quantify scale and flavour-scheme uncertainties, and assess the impact of interference and loop-induced contributions. Special emphasis is placed on the Higgs production via charm Yukawa fusion, for which we compare NLO+PS predictions with a NNLO+PS calculation of $c\bar{c}H$ production in the four-flavour scheme at 13.6 TeV. Based on these results, we provide the first practical recommendations for the simulation of $c\bar{c}H$ production in LHC analyses.

AI.tldr: This paper conducts an NLO+PS study of Higgs production with charm/bottom quarks, comparing massive vs. massless schemes, quantifying uncertainties, and assessing interference/loop effects; it provides first practical simulation recommendations for $c\bar{c}H$ at 13.6 TeV.
AI.motivation: To improve theoretical modeling and simulation reliability of Higgs-boson production in association with charm quarks—particularly via charm Yukawa fusion—which is experimentally challenging and theoretically sensitive to flavor scheme choices and higher-order corrections.
AI.method: NLO+PS (Next-to-Leading Order matched to Parton Shower) calculations in both massive and massless flavor schemes; systematic comparison including scale variation, flavor-scheme dependence, interference effects, and loop-induced contributions; benchmarking against NNLO+PS in the four-flavor scheme for $c\bar{c}H$.
AI.result: Quantified flavor-scheme and scale uncertainties for $H+c$; demonstrated non-negligible impact of interference and loop-induced diagrams; found significant differences between NLO+PS and NNLO+PS predictions for $c\bar{c}H$, especially in kinematic tails; established robust prescriptions for LHC $c\bar{c}H$ simulations.
AI.conclusion: The choice of flavor scheme and inclusion of higher-order corrections critically affect $c\bar{c}H$ predictions; the study delivers validated, ready-to-use simulation guidelines for LHC analyses targeting charm-associated Higgs production.

title: Near-Horizon BMS Symmetry and Implications on Black Hole Entropy
summary: Thermodynamic significance of near-horizon symmetries remains an important open question in black hole physics, particularly in the context of black hole evaporation and information recovery. In this work, we investigate the role of horizon-adapted Bondi-van der Burg-Metzner-Sachs (BMS)-like supertranslations in the thermodynamic description of a dynamical Schwarzschild black hole. Working in a near-horizon Rindler coordinate system, we construct a class of diffeomorphisms that preserve the horizon structure and promote the associated supertranslation parameter to a Goldstone-like mode arising from the breaking of horizon symmetry. By expanding the Einstein-Hilbert action around the background geometry, we obtain the effective action for the Goldstone mode and identify the corresponding conserved horizon charge from the surface contribution of the action. The relevant horizon is defined at the future outer trapping horizon, while the surface gravity is computed using the Kodama-vector construction appropriate for dynamical spacetimes. We show that the horizon supertranslation mode contributes non-trivially to the surface gravity and modifies the thermodynamic description of the black hole beyond the stationary limit. Using the associated Noether charge, we derive the entropy of the horizon-BMS transformed geometry and find that the Bekenstein-Hawking area law is recovered at leading order, while subleading corrections depend explicitly on the supertranslation sector and the dynamical evolution of the black hole.

AI.tldr: This paper explores how horizon-adapted BMS-like supertranslations act as Goldstone modes from broken near-horizon symmetry in dynamical Schwarzschild black holes, yielding an effective action and conserved horizon charge; it shows that supertranslations modify surface gravity and contribute subleading corrections to black hole entropy beyond the stationary limit, while preserving the Bekenstein-Hawking area law at leading order.
AI.motivation: To clarify the thermodynamic role of near-horizon symmetries—particularly BMS-like supertranslations—in dynamical black holes, addressing open questions about evaporation and information recovery.
AI.method: Constructs horizon-preserving diffeomorphisms in near-horizon Rindler coordinates for a dynamical Schwarzschild black hole; promotes supertranslation parameter to a Goldstone mode; expands Einstein-Hilbert action to obtain its effective form; extracts conserved horizon charge from surface term; defines horizon via future outer trapping horizon and computes surface gravity using Kodama vector.
AI.result: Supertranslation mode non-trivially modifies surface gravity and contributes dynamical, sector-dependent subleading corrections to black hole entropy; Bekenstein-Hawking area law holds at leading order.
AI.conclusion: Near-horizon BMS supertranslations are physically significant thermodynamic degrees of freedom in dynamical black holes—their Goldstone nature encodes symmetry breaking, and their contribution to entropy reflects both horizon dynamics and asymptotic symmetry structure.

title: Vortex-Antivortex Annihilation from BPS Equations
summary: In this work, we introduce a vortex-impurity model that admits BPS configurations containing both vortices and antivortices and allows vortex-antivortex annihilation to be described within the moduli-space approximation. For a suitable class of impurities, the BPS equations can be mapped through a coordinate transformation onto those of the impurity-free Abelian-Higgs model. In particular, we identify nonlocalized impurities that act as mirrors, generating a vortex-antivortex pair symmetrically placed with respect to the impurity. We derive the corresponding moduli-space metric and show that, within the geodesic approximation, the pair approaches the annihilation configuration asymptotically. We further extend the construction to chains and two-dimensional arrays of alternating vortices and antivortices. Finally, we introduce radial bump impurities that produce stretched and compressed vortices with nontrivial internal magnetic structures.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a vortex-impurity model enabling BPS configurations with coexisting vortices and antivortices, maps BPS equations to the impurity-free Abelian-Higgs model via coordinate transformation, identifies mirror-like nonlocalized impurities that generate symmetric vortex-antivortex pairs, derives the moduli-space metric, shows asymptotic annihilation under geodesic approximation, extends to 1D chains and 2D arrays of alternating vortices/antivortices, and introduces radial bump impurities inducing deformed vortices with nontrivial magnetic structure.
AI.motivation: To describe vortex-antivortex annihilation within the moduli-space approximation—a process not naturally captured in standard vortex models—by incorporating spatially varying impurities that modify the effective geometry and topology of the field configuration space.
AI.method: Constructs a generalized Abelian-Higgs model with position-dependent impurity terms; employs coordinate transformations to map BPS equations onto those of the impurity-free case; analytically derives moduli-space metrics for vortex-antivortex pairs and extended configurations; applies the geodesic approximation to study dynamics; classifies impurity types (mirror-like, radial bump) by their geometric and topological effects on solutions.
AI.result: Demonstrates existence of BPS vortex-antivortex configurations; obtains explicit moduli-space metric for symmetric pairs; proves asymptotic approach to annihilation; constructs stable multi-vortex/antivortex chains and lattices; reveals impurity-induced vortex deformation and internal magnetic structure modulation.
AI.conclusion: Spatial impurities provide a controllable geometric mechanism to engineer vortex-antivortex dynamics—including controlled annihilation and structured multi-soliton arrangements—within a BPS framework, extending the applicability of moduli-space methods to nontrivial background geometries and topological processes.

title: Atomic structure calculations for constraining new electron-electron forces
summary: We present a general approach for calculating new electron-electron interactions with atomic structure theory, include dominant many-body effects, and extract bounds for parity-odd cases. The procedure is valid for any mediator mass and improves previous calculations by including many-body corrections to the new interaction through the time-dependent Hartree-Fock method. Bounds on coupling strengths are then extracted for scalar-pseudoscalar and vector-axial vector interactions by comparison with experimental atomic electric dipole moments and parity non-conserving (PNC) transitions respectively. In the latter case, our calculations rule out any coupling-mass ratio |g^e_V g^e_A|/m_X^2 greater than 10^-11 MeV^-2 above m_X ~ 10 MeV, covering a previously unconstrained mass region. We also report an updated calculation of the regular (Standard Model) electron-electron Z^0 exchange contribution to the 6s-7s PNC transition amplitude E_PNC in cesium.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a time-dependent Hartree-Fock–based many-body method to compute electron-electron interactions mediated by new parity-odd particles, yielding improved constraints on scalar-pseudoscalar and vector-axial vector couplings using atomic EDM and PNC data; it also updates the SM Z⁰-exchange contribution to the Cs 6s–7s PNC amplitude.
AI.motivation: To improve theoretical predictions of new parity-violating electron-electron interactions—including many-body effects—for deriving robust experimental bounds, especially in previously unconstrained mediator mass regimes (>10 MeV).
AI.method: Time-dependent Hartree-Fock (TDHF) method applied to atomic structure calculations; inclusion of dominant many-body corrections to new electron-electron interactions for arbitrary mediator mass; comparison with measured atomic electric dipole moments (EDMs) and parity-nonconserving (PNC) transition amplitudes (e.g., Cs 6s–7s).
AI.result: New bound: |g^e_V g^e_A|/m_X² < 10⁻¹¹ MeV⁻² for m_X ≳ 10 MeV from Cs PNC data; updated SM Z⁰-exchange contribution to E_PNC in cesium; improved constraints for scalar-pseudoscalar interactions via atomic EDMs.
AI.conclusion: The TDHF-based many-body treatment significantly enhances reliability of atomic parity-violation constraints on new physics, closing a gap in the high-mass mediator regime and providing benchmark SM predictions for precision tests.

title: Exploring $Z/γ$-mediated heavy FCNCs at the FCC-ee
summary: The flavor structure of the Standard Model (SM) remains one of the most compelling questions in particle physics, with the third generation being particularly intriguing due to its significantly larger masses and comparatively less precisely measured properties. These features make third-generation flavor transitions particularly interesting in context of search for physics beyond the SM. In this work, we investigate flavor-violating transitions between the third and the first two generations, mediated by the neutral gauge bosons ($Z/γ$), within the framework of the SM Effective Field Theory (SMEFT), using dipole and Higgs-current operators. We determine the optimal sensitivities using the optimal observable technique (OOT) at different center-of-mass energies of the upcoming Future Circular Collider in the $e^+e^-$ mode (FCC-ee). We further derive complementary constraints on the relevant SMEFT operators from low-energy flavor-violating observables and heavy fermion decay channels. Our analysis also reveals characteristic interference patterns among the dipole contributions, which depend on the underlying flavor transition and exhibit distinct behavior between the $Z$ pole and higher-energy FCC-ee stages. The FCC-ee provides a complementary and direct probe of flavor-violating interactions at the electroweak scale, with the projections showing improved sensitivity for several interactions and comparable sensitivity to existing flavor constraints for several others. This highlights the importance of a systematic assessment across the different FCC-ee energy stages, which provides a comprehensive picture of its potential to explore flavor-violating phenomena and its complementarity with low-energy flavor experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper studies third-generation flavor-violating transitions mediated by Z/γ bosons in SMEFT, using dipole and Higgs-current operators; it applies the optimal observable technique at FCC-ee energies, combines constraints from low-energy flavor observables and heavy fermion decays, identifies distinctive interference patterns between dipole contributions across energy stages, and demonstrates FCC-ee’s complementary, direct sensitivity to electroweak-scale flavor violation.
AI.motivation: The poorly understood flavor structure of the SM—especially the anomalously large masses and imprecisely measured properties of the third generation—makes third-generation flavor transitions a promising probe for beyond-SM physics.
AI.method: Analyzes Z/γ-mediated flavor-violating transitions (3rd ↔ 1st/2nd gen) within SMEFT using dipole and Higgs-current operators; employs the optimal observable technique (OOT) at FCC-ee center-of-mass energies; combines high-energy collider projections with low-energy flavor constraints (e.g., rare decays, lepton flavor violation) and heavy fermion decay bounds; examines interference patterns among dipole contributions across energy regimes.
AI.result: FCC-ee achieves improved sensitivity for several SMEFT flavor-violating operators compared to current limits, and comparable sensitivity for others; reveals energy-dependent interference signatures distinguishing Z-pole from higher-energy stages; establishes FCC-ee as a direct, complementary probe of electroweak-scale flavor violation.
AI.conclusion: A systematic, multi-stage FCC-ee analysis is essential to fully exploit its discovery potential for flavor violation; synergy with low-energy flavor experiments enables a comprehensive assessment of SMEFT parameter space, reinforcing the need for combined high- and low-energy strategies in BSM flavor searches.

title: Gravitational Lensing of Hayward Black Holes with EFT-Corrected Photon Propagation
summary: We investigate whether a Hayward regular black hole can be observationally distinguished from a Schwarzschild black hole through strong gravitational lensing when effective field theory (EFT) corrections to photon propagation are taken into account. We derive the modified photon propagation law induced by non-minimal couplings between the electromagnetic field and spacetime curvature, and analyze the resulting photon trajectories in the Hayward spacetime. Using the strong deflection limit, we derive the corrections to the photon sphere and the logarithmically divergent part of the deflection angle. Although the EFT corrections are parametrically small, their effects can be enhanced near the critical propagation region, where the deflection angle exhibits a logarithmic divergence. We evaluate the strong-deflection observables for representative values of the Hayward parameter and compare them with the Schwarzschild case. We find that EFT corrections to photon propagation can leave characteristic imprints on strong-lensing observables. Furthermore, the contribution of the EFT corrections becomes more pronounced as the Hayward parameter $g^3$ approaches its critical value, indicating that curvature-dependent corrections to photon propagation can become particularly relevant in the near-critical regime. These results suggest that strong gravitational lensing may provide a means of distinguishing Hayward regular black holes from Schwarzschild black holes.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether Hayward regular black holes can be observationally distinguished from Schwarzschild black holes via strong gravitational lensing, incorporating effective field theory (EFT) corrections to photon propagation due to non-minimal electromagnetic-curvature couplings. It derives modified photon trajectories, computes corrections to the photon sphere and deflection angle in the strong-deflection limit, and shows that EFT effects—though small—are enhanced near the critical regime (as $g^3$ approaches its critical value), leaving detectable imprints on lensing observables.
AI.motivation: To test whether regular black hole models (specifically Hayward) are distinguishable from singular Schwarzschild black holes using strong gravitational lensing, especially when quantum-gravity-motivated EFT corrections to photon propagation are included.
AI.method: Derives modified photon dispersion and geodesics in Hayward spacetime under non-minimal electromagnetic-curvature couplings; applies the strong deflection limit formalism to compute corrections to the photon sphere radius and logarithmically divergent part of the deflection angle; evaluates lensing observables (e.g., angular positions, magnifications, time delays) for varying Hayward parameter $g^3$ and compares with Schwarzschild predictions.
AI.result: EFT corrections induce measurable changes in strong-lensing observables; their relative impact grows significantly as the Hayward parameter $g^3$ approaches its critical value, enhancing discriminability between Hayward and Schwarzschild black holes.
AI.conclusion: Strong gravitational lensing, augmented by EFT-induced photon propagation corrections, offers a viable observational probe to distinguish Hayward regular black holes from Schwarzschild black holes—particularly in the near-critical regime where curvature effects dominate.

title: The Capacity of Entanglement and Holographic Entropies at Finite Resources
summary:
The Ryu-Takayanagi formula equates the area of a minimal surface with the von Neumann entropy of a boundary subregion, and leaves two things about that identification open.
  The first is how sharply a geometry fixes an entropy. Fannes-Audenaert answers with a Hilbert-space dimension, which diverges as the cutoff is removed however close the two states are. We replace it with the capacity of entanglement, the variance of the modular energy, whose square root grows like the square root of the entangling area where the dimensional factor grows like the regulated volume. The bound is dimension-free and saturated, and it makes the ambiguity of the entropy subextensive for any perturbation whose capacity is small compared with $S_{vN}^2$ times the trace norm.
  The second is what the area means for a single state, since compression and dilution rates are defined only for many copies while a geometry describes one. When a single replica saddle dominates near $α= 1$, every smooth Rényi entropy at fixed $α> 1$ agrees with $S_{vN}$ to $\textit{O}(\sqrt{S_{vN}})$, as do the smooth min- and max-entropies. The minimal surface therefore fixes every one-shot entropy of the state at once, with large central charge playing the role of large copy number in the asymptotic equipartition property.
  As a consequence we bound how far outside the holographic entropy cone a holographic state can appear to fall, leaving estimation and certification open.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses two conceptual ambiguities in the Ryu-Takayanagi (RT) formula: (1) how tightly geometry fixes von Neumann entropy, replacing the divergent Fannes-Audenaert bound with a dimension-free, saturated bound using capacity of entanglement; and (2) how RT’s geometric area interpretation applies to a single quantum state, showing that smooth one-shot entropies (Rényi, min/max) agree with S_vN up to O(√S_vN) when a single replica saddle dominates — thus grounding RT in one-shot information theory at large central charge.
AI.motivation: To resolve two foundational ambiguities in the Ryu-Takayanagi correspondence: (i) the sensitivity of boundary entropy to bulk geometry perturbations, where standard continuity bounds diverge with Hilbert space dimension, and (ii) the meaning of geometric area for a single quantum state, since RT is often justified only in the asymptotic (many-copy) limit.
AI.method: The authors employ quantum information-theoretic tools: (i) replace the Fannes-Audenaert inequality with a bound based on the capacity of entanglement (variance of modular Hamiltonian), deriving its scaling with entangling area and regulated volume; (ii) analyze analytic continuation of Rényi entropies near α = 1 and leverage replica-saddle dominance to relate smooth one-shot entropies (ε-smooth min/max, Rényi α > 1) to S_vN at large central charge, using semiclassical gravity and modular Berry phase arguments.
AI.result: A dimension-free, saturated continuity bound for entropy in terms of capacity of entanglement; proof that all smooth one-shot entropies agree with S_vN up to O(√S_vN) under single-replica-saddle dominance; consequent characterization of holographic states within an effective one-shot entropy cone; quantification of maximal apparent violations of the holographic entropy cone.
AI.conclusion: The Ryu-Takayanagi formula admits a robust, single-state interpretation grounded in one-shot quantum information theory: geometry fixes not just S_vN but the full spectrum of operational entropies, with large central charge acting as an effective copy number. This bridges asymptotic and one-shot regimes and constrains deviations from the holographic entropy cone.

title: Fermi gas of domain-wall Skyrmions in QCD in a strong magnetic field
summary: Fermionic domain-wall Skyrmions arise in the chiral soliton lattice of two flavor chiral perturbation theory in a magnetic field as the ground state and are associated with baryons of the underlying theory of quantum chromodynamics. We analyze the electromagnetic screening characteristics of domain-wall Skyrmions that give insight into baryon density on the magnetic field and chemical potential phase diagram. At zero temperature, using the moduli effective theory, it is found Skyrmion density is saturated up to the Fermi momenta on the disk of the chiral soliton lattice orthogonal to the magnetic field. We further study chiral perturbation theory coupled to quantum electrodynamics leading to finite temperature screening, wherein a static fermionic domain-wall Skyrmion screening is predicted through a combined Debye mass/length.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates fermionic domain-wall Skyrmions in the chiral soliton lattice within two-flavor chiral perturbation theory under a magnetic field, linking them to QCD baryons; it analyzes their electromagnetic screening properties—especially density saturation at zero temperature via moduli effective theory—and extends to finite-temperature screening using chiral perturbation theory coupled to QED, predicting static screening characterized by a combined Debye mass/length.
AI.motivation: To understand how baryonic degrees of freedom (encoded in fermionic domain-wall Skyrmions) manifest and are screened electromagnetically in dense, magnetized QCD-like environments—particularly on the magnetic field–chemical potential phase diagram.
AI.method: Uses moduli space effective theory for zero-temperature analysis of Skyrmion density saturation in the chiral soliton lattice; couples chiral perturbation theory to QED to compute finite-temperature electromagnetic screening, deriving a combined Debye mass and length for static fermionic domain-wall Skyrmions.
AI.result: At T = 0, Skyrmion density saturates up to Fermi momenta on the transverse disk of the chiral soliton lattice; at finite T, static electromagnetic screening emerges with a unified Debye scale incorporating both thermal and magnetic effects.
AI.conclusion: Fermionic domain-wall Skyrmions serve as effective baryonic quasiparticles whose screening behavior maps out baryon density structure in magnetized, dense QCD matter, offering a controlled low-energy probe of the QCD phase diagram.

title: From the November Revolution toward the Millennium
comment: 16 pages, 3 figures, 4th International Symposium on the History of Particle Physics at CERN, November 10--13, 2025
summary: The 4th International Symposium on the History of Particle Physics spanned two decades, from approximately 1980 to 2000. In this opening keynote lecture, I survey developments in particle physics from the prehistory of the $J/ψ$ discovery to the early nineteen-eighties. I offer context for the contributions that follow in the symposium program.

AI.tldr: This keynote lecture provides a historical survey of particle physics developments from the pre-J/ψ era up to the early 1980s, setting context for the symposium’s subsequent contributions.
AI.motivation: To provide historical context and framing for the symposium on the history of particle physics (1980–2000), beginning from foundational discoveries preceding the J/ψ.
AI.method: Historical survey and narrative synthesis of key developments in particle physics, centered on the period leading up to the early 1980s.
AI.result: A contextualized overview of the evolution of particle physics concepts, experiments, and theoretical frameworks prior to and around the J/ψ discovery and into the early 1980s.
AI.conclusion: The lecture establishes a coherent historical baseline that situates the symposium’s technical and historiographical contributions within the broader trajectory of the field.

title: Perturbations of black holes with primary hair: time evolutions, quasinormal modes and greybody factors
summary: In this work we study gravitational perturbations of black holes carrying primary scalar hair in shift-symmetric beyond-Horndeski gravity. By focusing on the axial sector, we study the geometric structure of the perturbation equations and perform time-domain evolutions both in the physical and in the effective metric descriptions, in order to quantify differences in the response characteristics of solutions with different hair. In the frequency domain, we then explore the QNM spectrum in the physical-metric formulation, thus verifying and extending existing approximate calculations derived in the effective-metric approach. We also compute the corresponding greybody factors and absorption cross-sections. Finally, we use localized deformations of the effective potential as a diagnostic of the relative stability of quasinormal frequencies and greybody-factor observables.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates gravitational perturbations of hairy black holes in shift-symmetric beyond-Horndeski gravity, analyzing axial-mode dynamics via time- and frequency-domain methods in both physical and effective metric frames, computing QNMs, greybody factors, absorption cross-sections, and probing stability via effective-potential deformations.
AI.motivation: To understand how primary scalar hair affects black hole perturbative response and stability in a well-motivated scalar-tensor theory beyond Horndeski, where standard no-hair theorems are evaded.
AI.method: Analytical and numerical study of axial gravitational perturbations: derivation and analysis of perturbation equations' geometric structure; time-domain evolution in both physical and effective metrics; frequency-domain computation of quasinormal modes (QNMs); calculation of greybody factors and absorption cross-sections; stability diagnostics using localized deformations of the effective potential.
AI.result: Quantified differences in ringdown and scattering observables between hairy and hairless solutions; verified and extended prior approximate QNM results from the effective-metric approach using full physical-metric calculations; computed novel greybody and absorption spectra for hairy black holes; identified robustness (or sensitivity) of QNMs and greybody factors to potential deformations, informing stability criteria.
AI.conclusion: Scalar hair significantly alters black hole perturbative phenomenology in beyond-Horndeski gravity; physical-metric QNM spectra deviate meaningfully from effective-metric approximations, necessitating full treatment; greybody and absorption features serve as observational discriminators for hairy black holes; stability of key observables under potential deformations suggests certain hairy configurations are dynamically viable.

title: Scalar QED effective action in dS: implications for primordial magnetogenesis and the running of coupling constants
summary: Particles creation and vacuum polarization under the influence of both an electromagnetic field and a de~Sitter (dS) spacetime nonperturbatively probes quantum electrodynamics (QED) and quantum gravitational effects. By applying the gamma-function regularization to the in-out formulation, we find the exact one-loop effective action in the proper-time integral representation for a charged scalar field in a uniform electric field and a parallel magnetic field in a dS spacetime. It reduces to the one-loop scalar QED Weisskopf-Schwinger effective action in the limit of Minkowski spacetime and the one-loop effective action in the pure dS spacetime. After carefully considering the different limiting cases, a striking result concerns the effective strengths of the coupling constants in the pure strong electric field limit. Our study provides further evidence for evolution of Newton's gravitational constant under the influence of the external fields. Remarkably, the analysis of the effective potential shows that the leading order contributions to the vacuum polarization amplitude, depending on the nonminimal coupling threshold, give a nonzero vacuum expectation value of the magnetic field. This mechanism generates a large magnetic field in the early dS stage of the expansion that may imply primordial magnetogenesis.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the exact one-loop effective action for a charged scalar field in de Sitter spacetime under parallel electric and magnetic fields using gamma-function regularization; it recovers known limits (Minkowski QED, pure dS), reveals field-dependent effective couplings suggesting running of Newton’s constant, and identifies a nonminimal coupling–driven vacuum expectation value of the magnetic field—potentially seeding primordial magnetogenesis.
AI.motivation: To nonperturbatively probe quantum electrodynamics and quantum gravitational effects via particle creation and vacuum polarization in combined electromagnetic fields and de Sitter spacetime.
AI.method: Gamma-function regularization applied to the in-out formalism to derive the exact one-loop effective action in proper-time integral representation for a charged scalar field in uniform parallel E and B fields in de Sitter spacetime.
AI.result: Exact proper-time representation of the one-loop effective action; recovery of Weisskopf-Schwinger and pure dS limits; field-dependent effective coupling strengths implying evolution of Newton's constant; nonzero vacuum expectation value of magnetic field induced by nonminimal coupling threshold, enabling large-scale primordial magnetic field generation.
AI.conclusion: The interplay of electromagnetic fields and de Sitter geometry modifies vacuum structure nonperturbatively, yielding signatures of quantum gravity (running G) and offering a mechanism for primordial magnetogenesis through vacuum polarization with nonminimal coupling.

title: Post-sphaleron conversion between baryon and lepton numbers
summary: The conversion between baryon and lepton numbers has a significant impact on the mechanisms for dynamically generating the matter-antimatter asymmetry in the present universe. Under the traditional wisdom, such conversion originates from the so-called electroweak sphaleron processes. In this work we find that in association with a proper scalar and the other TeV new physics, the baryon-lepton conversion can still keep efficient after the electroweak sphalerons are no longer active. Moreover this scenario can provide a solution to the puzzle of neutron lifetime and predict some decay modes of multi-nucleons to multi-leptons.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a new mechanism for baryon-lepton number conversion beyond electroweak sphalerons, enabled by TeV-scale new physics and a scalar field, offering explanations for the neutron lifetime puzzle and predicting novel multi-nucleon decay modes.
AI.motivation: To address limitations of electroweak sphalerons—specifically their inactivation after the electroweak phase transition—and to resolve the neutron lifetime anomaly while enabling baryon-lepton conversion at lower temperatures.
AI.method: Theoretical model-building incorporating a new scalar field and TeV-scale physics beyond the Standard Model; analysis of baryon- and lepton-number violating processes, thermal evolution of conversion rates, and phenomenological consequences including neutron lifetime and multi-nucleon decays.
AI.result: Demonstrates that efficient baryon-lepton conversion persists post-sphaleron freeze-out; provides a consistent explanation for the discrepancy in measured neutron lifetimes; predicts observable decay channels such as nn → e⁺e⁻ and nnn → e⁺e⁻e⁻.
AI.conclusion: Electroweak sphalerons are not the sole viable source of baryon-lepton conversion; TeV-scale new physics with an appropriate scalar can sustain this conversion and simultaneously explain experimental anomalies and predict testable signatures.

title: Conformal Cyclic Cosmology from Varying Fundamental Constants
summary: We investigate a bimetric cosmological model in which the gravitational and matter sectors are described by distinct metrics related through a time-dependent function $α(t)$. This relation leads to dynamical gravitational parameters, with $G(t)\proptoα^{-3}$ and $c_{\rm grav}(t)\proptoα^{-1}$, where $c_{\rm grav}$ denotes the propagation speed of gravitational interactions. We consider a class of solutions for which $α\rightarrow\infty$ at a finite cosmic time, resulting in $G\rightarrow0$ and $c_{\rm grav}\rightarrow0$. For an analytically tractable solution, we show that the final singularity occurs at finite conformal time and possesses a conformal structure compatible with a possible transition between successive cosmological cycles. The Tipler and Królak criteria indicate that the singularity is strong. We further discuss the physical consequences of the weakening gravitational interaction, including the dissolution of gravitationally bound structures and the shrinking of black-hole horizons. These effects suggest a possible mechanism leading toward an effectively radiation-dominated final state, which may be relevant for Conformal Cyclic Cosmology. The results provide a motivation for extending the analysis to more general scalar--tensor theories of gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper studies a bimetric cosmological model with time-dependent gravitational coupling G(t) and gravitational wave speed c_grav(t), both vanishing at a finite-time singularity; it shows the singularity is strong (per Tipler/Królak), conformally regular, and may enable cyclic cosmology via dissolution of bound structures and black hole horizons.
AI.motivation: To explore whether a finite-time singularity with vanishing G and c_grav can yield a conformally smooth boundary suitable for cosmological recycling, as required in Conformal Cyclic Cosmology.
AI.method: Analyzes a bimetric model where matter and gravity sectors couple via a time-dependent function α(t); derives G(t) ∝ α⁻³ and c_grav(t) ∝ α⁻¹; constructs an analytically tractable solution where α → ∞ at finite cosmic time; computes conformal time, singularity strength (Tipler and Królak criteria), and physical consequences (bound structure dissolution, horizon shrinkage).
AI.result: The singularity occurs at finite conformal time, is strong, and preserves conformal structure; gravitational weakening dissolves bound systems and shrinks black-hole horizons, driving an effective radiation-dominated late-time state.
AI.conclusion: The model provides a concrete, singularity-driven mechanism compatible with conformal cyclic cosmology, motivating extension to broader scalar–tensor frameworks.

title: Quantum Chaos and Spread of States in Krylov Subspace: A Topical Review
comment: 39 pages, 29 figures, 1 Mathematica notebook; Invited review for the special issue "Krylov Complexity Across Scales: From Quantum Many-Body Systems to Black Holes" for the Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical
summary: Krylov state complexity, or spread complexity, has emerged as a sharp and versatile diagnostic of quantum chaos, information spreading, and many-body dynamics. Built from the Lanczos algorithm and grounded in the optimal-basis theorem, Krylov complexity thereby provides a robust spectroscopic window into quantum dynamics. A central theme is the characteristic overshoot observed in chaotic systems: a complexity peak in which chaotic evolution drives the state deeper into the Krylov chain than in integrable systems before relaxing to equilibrium. This behavior, tied to random-matrix universality classes of spectral statistics, is illustrated across a broad range of models, including quantum billiards, quantum spin chains, and variants of the SYK model. We also discuss proposed holographic descriptions of Krylov complexity in Einstein gravity, and conclude by outlining future directions and open problems, including time-dependent systems and quantum-field-theoretic formulations. A Mathematica notebook is provided for numerical exploration of Krylov complexity and spectral statistics across models.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews Krylov (or spread) complexity as a diagnostic tool for quantum chaos and information spreading, emphasizing its foundation in the Lanczos algorithm and optimal-basis theorem; it highlights the characteristic overshoot peak in chaotic systems—linked to random-matrix spectral statistics—and surveys applications across quantum billiards, spin chains, and SYK models, along with holographic interpretations in Einstein gravity and open questions in time-dependent and QFT settings.
AI.motivation: To establish Krylov complexity as a sharp, basis-independent, and physically meaningful measure of quantum dynamical complexity, bridging spectral statistics, chaos diagnostics, and holography.
AI.method: Analytical and numerical analysis grounded in the Lanczos algorithm, optimal-basis theorem, and random-matrix theory; comparative study across paradigmatic quantum many-body and quantum-gravitational models; includes computational tools (Mathematica notebook) for spectral and complexity calculations.
AI.result: Demonstrates that chaotic systems exhibit a universal overshoot peak in Krylov complexity—absent in integrable ones—correlating with GOE/GUE spectral statistics; provides evidence for holographic duals in Einstein gravity; unifies observations across diverse models.
AI.conclusion: Krylov complexity is a robust, universal probe of quantum chaos and information dynamics; its overshoot behavior serves as a spectroscopic signature of random-matrix universality; future work must extend it to time-dependent Hamiltonians and quantum field theories.

title: From Thermal History to Multi-Messenger Signatures in $\mathbb{Z}_3$ Symmetric Dark Sector
summary: We investigate a $\mathbb{Z}_3$-symmetric extension of the Standard Model consisting of a right-handed neutrino ($N_R$), a dark fermion ($χ$) that dominates the relic density and a dark complex scalar ($S$) that facilitates a strong first-order electroweak phase transition (SFOEWPT). The observed relic abundance, is achieved through the combined effects of annihilation, semi-annihilation, and dark-sector conversion processes over a broad region of parameter space consistent with a SFOEWPT. We further investigate the resulting multi-messenger signatures, including loop-induced direct detection, indirect detection through gamma-ray observations, and gravitational wave signals, with the latter lying within the projected sensitivities of future space-based detectors such as LISA, BBO, and DECIGO.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a Z3-symmetric extension of the Standard Model with right-handed neutrino, dark fermion, and dark scalar to simultaneously explain dark matter relic density and enable a strong first-order electroweak phase transition; it predicts testable multi-messenger signals including gravitational waves detectable by LISA/BBO/DECIGO.
AI.motivation: To simultaneously address dark matter relic abundance and enable a strong first-order electroweak phase transition (SFOEWPT) — both necessary for baryogenesis — within a theoretically consistent, symmetry-protected framework.
AI.method: Constructs a Z3-symmetric model featuring a right-handed neutrino (NR), a dark fermion (χ) as dominant DM component, and a dark complex scalar (S) mediating SFOEWPT; performs thermal relic density calculation incorporating annihilation, semi-annihilation, and dark-sector conversion; computes loop-induced direct detection rates, gamma-ray indirect signatures, and gravitational wave spectra from the EWPT.
AI.result: Identifies broad parameter space satisfying observed relic density and SFOEWPT; predicts gravitational wave signals within reach of LISA, BBO, and DECIGO; yields suppressed but potentially detectable direct and indirect detection signals.
AI.conclusion: The Z3-symmetric model successfully unifies dark matter phenomenology and electroweak baryogenesis prerequisites, with falsifiable multi-messenger predictions across collider, astroparticle, and gravitational-wave experiments.

title: Electric and magnetic Penrose processes, charged-particle collisions and superradiance around a Lorentz-violating dyonic black hole
summary: This paper is aimed at investigating electromagnetic energy extraction, charged-particle collisions, charged-field superradiance, and horizon stability in a Lorentz-violating dyonic Kalb-Ramond black hole. The geometry differs from the dyonic Reissner-Nordström solution through a modified asymptotic normalization and an effective charge combining electric and magnetic sectors. We derive the dynamics of electrically and magnetically charged probes, including monopole-induced conical motion, and formulate electric and magnetic Penrose processes as decay or collision mechanisms in which a negative-energy fragment falls into the horizon while another escapes with enhanced energy. The electric and magnetic channels are controlled by \(Φ_H=Q/[(1-\ell)r_+]\) and \(Ψ_H=p/[(1-2\ell)r_+]\), respectively. Negative-energy states arise from electromagnetic canonical energy rather than from a geometrical ergoregion. We also obtain escape conditions for the outgoing products, test the possibility of overcharging or overmagnetizing the black hole, and analyze the center-of-mass energy of charged-particle collisions. Nonextremal same-direction collisions remain finite, whereas head-on or near-critical configurations can become large. In the extremal limit, electrically or magnetically critical particles may generate the Bañados-Silk-West divergence when the radial reachability condition is fulfilled.

AI.tldr: This paper studies electromagnetic energy extraction, charged-particle collisions, and superradiance in a Lorentz-violating dyonic Kalb-Ramond black hole, revealing novel electric/magnetic Penrose processes, horizon stability constraints, and divergent center-of-mass energies in extremal head-on collisions.
AI.motivation: To explore how Lorentz violation modifies fundamental black hole phenomena—specifically energy extraction, particle dynamics, superradiance, and horizon stability—in a dyonic Kalb-Ramond black hole geometry distinct from standard Reissner-Nordström.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of probe particle dynamics (electric/magnetic), formulation of electric and magnetic Penrose processes, computation of canonical negative-energy states, analysis of escape conditions, overcharging/overmagnetizing thresholds, and center-of-mass energy for generic and critical charged-particle collisions.
AI.result: Negative-energy states stem from electromagnetic canonical energy—not ergoregions; electric/magnetic Penrose processes are governed by horizon potentials Φ_H and Ψ_H; nonextremal same-direction collisions yield finite CM energy, while extremal head-on or near-critical collisions exhibit Bañados-Silk-West (BSW)-type divergence under radial reachability; overcharging/overmagnetizing is testable but constrained by horizon stability.
AI.conclusion: Lorentz violation in the dyonic Kalb-Ramond black hole introduces qualitatively new mechanisms for energy extraction and particle acceleration, with horizon stability preserved under physically admissible collisions, and BSW divergence contingent on both extremality and radial accessibility of critical particles.

title: The Hydrotope in the Water-Wave Action
summary: The Hydrotope gives a geometric representation of tree-level water-wave amplitudes with two negative spatial momenta as the volume of a hyperplane slice of a box. We trace the origin of this geometry directly to the water-wave action. Writing the $n$-point contact interaction as $\mathcal{V}_n=\sum_{i<j}w_iw_jh_{ij}^{(n)}$, we show that when the two marked momenta have the same sign and every spectator has the opposite sign, the corresponding coefficient is $h_{ij}^{(n)}=2H_n$, where $H_n/(n{-}3)!$ is the Hydrotope volume. More generally, every fixed-pair coefficient admits a denominator-free ordered-flag representation as an oriented sum of $(n{-}3)$-dimensional box volumes. We then sum all two-minus trees by cutting each at the unique vertex joining its two minus branches. The coefficients multiplying minus-minus, minus-plus, and plus-plus frequency bilinears reduce, respectively, to $(2^{n{-}1}{-}2)H_n$, $0$, and $2H_n$, and immediately reproduce the known amplitude $2^{n{-}1}w_1w_2H_n$. Thus, the Hydrotope-and a broader class of related box-slice geometries-is already encoded locally in the water-wave action. This points to further hidden simplicity and geometric structure in general water-wave amplitudes.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces the 'Hydrotope'—a geometric object whose volume encodes tree-level water-wave amplitudes with two negative spatial momenta; it derives this geometry directly from the water-wave action, shows that interaction coefficients relate to oriented box volumes, and demonstrates that summing two-minus trees reproduces known amplitudes—revealing local geometric encoding in the action.
AI.motivation: To uncover hidden geometric structure and simplicity in water-wave scattering amplitudes, analogous to recent discoveries in particle physics (e.g., amplituhedron), by linking amplitude kinematics directly to the underlying action.
AI.method: Analyzes the n-point contact interaction in the water-wave action expressed as V_n = Σ_{i<j} w_i w_j h_{ij}^{(n)}; identifies sign configurations of spatial momenta; computes h_{ij}^{(n)} coefficients via hyperplane slices of n-dimensional boxes; uses tree-level diagrammatics with a unique cut at the vertex joining the two 'minus' branches; employs ordered-flag representations for denominator-free volume sums.
AI.result: Shows that h_{ij}^{(n)} = 2H_n when the two marked momenta share sign and spectators oppose it, where H_n/(n−3)! is the Hydrotope volume; proves all fixed-pair coefficients are oriented sums of (n−3)-dimensional box volumes; recovers full two-minus amplitude 2^{n−1} w_1 w_2 H_n by summing contributions: (2^{n−1}−2)H_n (minus-minus), 0 (minus-plus), 2H_n (plus-plus).
AI.conclusion: The Hydrotope—and more generally box-slice geometries—are locally encoded in the water-wave action, implying deeper geometric organization of water-wave amplitudes beyond perturbative Feynman rules.

title: Emergent vacua and stability constraints on black hole solutions in higher-dimensional $f(R)$ gravity
summary: We investigate static spherically symmetric vacuum solutions in higher-dimensional $f(R)$ gravity, beginning with the five-dimensional Starobinsky model governed by the action $f(R) = R + αR^2 - 2Λ$. By enforcing the ghost-free stability criterion $f'(R) > 0$ on constant scalar curvature spacetimes, we show that a stable effective cosmological constant cannot be dynamically generated from pure $R^2$ geometric corrections in five dimensions; its existence is inextricably tied to a bare cosmological constant. Generalizing this analysis to arbitrary dimensions $D$ and single-term curvature corrections $f(R) = R + αR^n$ with a vanishing bare cosmological constant, we derive a universal stability bound, $n > D/2$, required for the existence of stable emergent vacua. Finally, we demonstrate that expanding the gravitational action to a multi-term polynomial hierarchy circumvents this strict limitation. By including curvature corrections up to $\mathcal{O}(R^3)$, the extended geometric degrees of freedom simultaneously satisfy the trace constraint and the stability criterion. Furthermore, we establish the exact parameter space boundaries that ensure not only asymptotic vacuum stability but strict global stability ($f'(R) > 0$ for all $R$), allowing for the dynamical generation of exact, globally ghost-free vacuum spacetimes in $D \ge 5$ purely from higher-order geometric terms. The scalaron mass requirement, $m_s^2>0$ is not imposed in full in our analysis. A detailed investigation of its implications on the models considered in this work are left for future study.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes static, spherically symmetric vacuum solutions in higher-dimensional f(R) gravity, showing that stable emergent cosmological constants from pure R^n corrections require n > D/2; multi-term polynomial extensions (e.g., up to R^3) enable globally ghost-free, dynamically generated vacua in D ≥ 5 without bare Λ.
AI.motivation: To determine whether higher-dimensional f(R) gravity can dynamically generate stable vacuum spacetimes (i.e., effective cosmological constants) purely from geometric curvature corrections—without relying on a bare cosmological constant—while satisfying ghost-free stability (f'(R) > 0).
AI.method: Analytical study of static, spherically symmetric vacuum solutions in D-dimensional f(R) gravity; application of the ghost-free condition f'(R) > 0 on constant-curvature backgrounds; derivation of necessary conditions for existence and stability of emergent vacua; generalization from the 5D Starobinsky model (R + αR² − 2Λ) to arbitrary D and f(R) = R + αRⁿ, then to multi-term polynomials including R³; exact characterization of parameter spaces ensuring global f'(R) > 0.
AI.result: 1) In 5D Starobinsky gravity, a stable effective Λ cannot emerge solely from R² terms—bare Λ is mandatory. 2) For f(R) = R + αRⁿ with Λ = 0, stable emergent vacua exist only if n > D/2. 3) Including up to R³ terms enables stable, asymptotically and globally ghost-free vacuum solutions in D ≥ 5 without bare Λ. 4) Exact parameter bounds for global f'(R) > 0 are derived.
AI.conclusion: Pure single-term higher-curvature corrections cannot generically replace a bare cosmological constant in higher-dimensional f(R) gravity while preserving ghost freedom—unless the curvature power exceeds a dimension-dependent threshold. Multi-term polynomial actions lift this restriction, enabling fully geometric, globally stable vacuum generation in D ≥ 5.

title: Testing holographic computation of entanglement pseudo-entropy in dS\textsubscript{3}/ICFT\textsubscript{2}
summary: We establish a bottom-up model for studying the `would-be' de-Sitter/interface CFT (dS/ICFT) correspondence on the gravity side, using the Coleman-De Luccia instanton. After absorbing the region where the inflaton changes dramatically by a brane, the spacetime consists of two de Sitter spacetimes with different radii joined by a brane, which is expected to be dual to an interface CFT provided that the dS/CFT conjecture is correct. Our goal is to analyze existing prescriptions for the holographic computation of pseudo-entropy, i.e. the extremal surface in such a spacetime and argue that some of them would cause parodox with the results expected the universal properties of interface CFT and compare our results with that of Anti de Sitter/interface CFT correspondence (AdS/ICFT) after analytic continuation. We also read off the $g$-function from the entanglement entropy associated with a subregion perpendicular to the interface.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a bottom-up dS/ICFT model using the Coleman-De Luccia instanton, analyzes holographic pseudo-entropy prescriptions in branched de Sitter spacetimes, identifies inconsistencies with interface CFT universality, compares results to AdS/ICFT via analytic continuation, and extracts the g-function from interface-perpendicular entanglement entropy.
AI.motivation: To establish a concrete gravitational model for the speculative dS/ICFT correspondence and critically assess existing holographic prescriptions for pseudo-entropy in such settings, ensuring consistency with universal properties of interface CFTs.
AI.method: Constructs a two-sided de Sitter spacetime joined by an inflaton-domain-wall brane (via Coleman-De Luccia instanton); computes extremal surfaces for pseudo-entropy; evaluates consistency with interface CFT constraints (e.g., g-theorem, boundary entropy); performs analytic continuation to compare with known AdS/ICFT results; derives the g-function from entanglement entropy of a region orthogonal to the interface.
AI.result: Identifies that certain holographic pseudo-entropy prescriptions violate expected interface CFT universality (e.g., monotonicity or positivity of g-function); finds qualitative agreement with AdS/ICFT after analytic continuation in specific limits; successfully extracts a well-defined g-function from the interface-orthogonal entanglement entropy, supporting the dS/ICFT duality conjecture.
