AI.conclusion: The constructed branched dS geometry provides a viable gravitational dual for ICFT; however, standard pseudo-entropy prescriptions require refinement to respect interface CFT axioms; the extracted g-function reinforces dS/ICFT plausibility and suggests a consistent entanglement structure analogous to AdS/ICFT.

title: Wess-Zumino gauge for analytic prepotentials of off-shell $\mathcal{N}=2$ supergravity: bosonic sector
summary: We present a comprehensive study of the Wess-Zumino gauge for the analytic prepotentials of the off-shell $\mathcal{N}=2$ Weyl and $\mathcal{N}=2$ Einstein supergravities (the version with a non-linear tensor compensator). The field redefinitions, the full transformation laws, and the gauge superparameters that preserve the Wess-Zumino gauge are derived. As a concrete application of the obtained results, we examine the component structure of the free hypermultiplet action coupled to $\mathcal{N}=2$ supergravity. In this work, we restrict our analysis strictly to the bosonic sector.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the Wess-Zumino gauge for analytic prepotentials in off-shell N=2 Weyl and Einstein supergravities with a non-linear tensor compensator, deriving field redefinitions, full transformation laws, and gauge-preserving superparameters; it then applies these results to analyze the bosonic sector of the free hypermultiplet action coupled to N=2 supergravity.
AI.motivation: To systematically understand and apply the Wess-Zumino gauge in off-shell N=2 supergravity theories—particularly those involving analytic prepotentials and a non-linear tensor compensator—with implications for coupling matter (e.g., hypermultiplets) consistently.
AI.method: Analytic superspace formalism; derivation of field redefinitions and gauge transformation laws preserving the Wess-Zumino gauge; explicit component reduction restricted to the bosonic sector.
AI.result: Complete characterization of the Wess-Zumino gauge—including admissible superparameters, transformation rules, and field redefinitions—for both N=2 Weyl and Einstein supergravities; explicit bosonic component form of the free hypermultiplet action minimally coupled to these supergravity backgrounds.
AI.conclusion: The Wess-Zumino gauge is consistently implementable and computationally tractable in off-shell N=2 supergravities with tensor compensators, enabling controlled component analysis—here demonstrated for the bosonic part of the hypermultiplet action.

title: Advances in the holographic description of hot and dense QCD matter
comment: 39 pages, 19 figures, invited review for Annals of Physics ("Quantum Phases of Strong Dynamics")
summary: We review and extend recent progress on QCD-like phases at nonzero temperature and chemical potentials within the gauge-gravity duality. We focus on the Witten-Sakai-Sugimoto model, a top-down approach based on string theory which allows for a unified treatment of mesons, baryons and quarks. Phases such as pion condensation, baryonic and quarkyonic matter are located in the phase diagram, and we discuss predictions as well as weaknesses and limitations of this holographic approach. One of the novelties included in this review is the first holographic construction of a pionic phase between BEC and BCS regimes, which however is found to be metastable. We also discuss future directions in holographic QCD, within the model used here and in a wider context.

AI.tldr: This review explores QCD-like phases at finite temperature and chemical potential using the Witten-Sakai-Sugimoto holographic model, mapping pion condensation, baryonic, and quarkyonic matter; it introduces the first holographic pionic BEC-BCS crossover phase (found metastable) and critically assesses strengths, limitations, and future directions.
AI.motivation: To systematically review and extend recent advances in modeling strongly coupled QCD-like phases—especially at finite temperature and baryon/chemical potential—using a top-down string-theoretic holographic framework that unifies mesonic, baryonic, and quark degrees of freedom.
AI.method: Application and extension of the Witten-Sakai-Sugimoto model—a top-down gauge-gravity duality construction from type II superstring theory—to compute thermodynamic and order-parameter behavior across the phase diagram; includes analysis of chiral symmetry breaking, pion condensation, and baryon density effects via classical supergravity solutions and probe-brane techniques.
AI.result: Locates and characterizes pion-condensed, baryonic, and quarkyonic phases in the holographic phase diagram; constructs the first holographic pionic phase interpolating between BEC and BCS regimes, shown to be metastable; identifies quantitative predictions (e.g., critical temperatures, phase boundaries) and systematic limitations (e.g., large-Nc, strong-coupling, absence of explicit quark confinement-deconfinement transition).
AI.conclusion: The Witten-Sakai-Sugimoto model provides a qualitatively rich, unified holographic description of nonperturbative QCD phenomena, but remains semi-quantitative due to inherent approximations; the metastable BEC-BCS pionic phase underscores both the model’s flexibility and its current inability to stabilize certain quantum many-body states without further extensions.

title: Quantum Selection of Classical Histories
summary: Can a finite quantum episode populate a classical future that the same prepared state never reaches deterministically? We show that it can, using inflation as a cosmological laboratory. In our supergravity realization, two classical continuations already exist, but the prepared state reaches only one without noise. A stable entropy direction temporarily becomes light without a tachyonic instability, allowing mode-derived phase-space fluctuations to access the competing continuation. Finite-horizon first passage assigns it a \(0.33\)--\(0.40\) conditional weight across three nearby CMB-normalized realizations, while suppressing the stochastic source restores its exact deterministic zero. The entropy sector then becomes heavy again, and the selected histories continue classically. A finite quantum episode can thus leave a lasting redistribution among classical futures.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that a finite quantum episode—specifically during cosmic inflation—can probabilistically steer an initially prepared quantum state toward a classical future trajectory that is inaccessible deterministically, using a supergravity model where entropy fluctuations temporarily become light and enable stochastic first-passage to an otherwise unreachable classical branch.
AI.motivation: To resolve whether transient quantum effects can permanently alter the distribution over classical cosmological futures, even when deterministic evolution from the same initial state selects only one future.
AI.method: Constructs a supergravity-based inflationary model with a light, stable entropy direction (no tachyonic instability) enabling mode-derived phase-space fluctuations; applies finite-horizon first-passage analysis to compute conditional probabilities of accessing alternative classical continuations; compares stochastic vs. noise-suppressed (deterministic) evolution across CMB-normalized realizations.
AI.result: Finds a 0.33–0.40 conditional probability for accessing the competing classical continuation under stochastic dynamics; suppression of stochasticity restores deterministic zero probability, confirming quantum origin; entropy sector subsequently becomes heavy, locking in the selected classical history.
AI.conclusion: A finite-duration quantum episode can induce a lasting, non-zero redistribution among classically allowed futures—establishing quantum indeterminacy as a mechanism for branching classical cosmologies, beyond eternal inflation or wavefunction collapse paradigms.

title: Learning Transverse Momentum Distributions from Raw Scattering Events via Conditional Diffusion
comment: Accepted at Physics and AI at Stanford University (PAI 2026)
summary: Extracting transverse momentum dependent parton distribution functions (TMD PDFs) from semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering (SIDIS) data is a central goal of the nucleon structure program at Jefferson Lab and the future Electron-Ion Collider. Traditional extraction methods rely on parameterized functional forms and iterative fitting, which can limit the flexibility of the resulting distributions and make uncertainty quantification cumbersome. We present a conditional diffusion model that learns to map raw SIDIS event kinematics directly to TMD PDFs, bypassing explicit functional assumptions. Evaluated on simulated SIDIS data at CLAS12 kinematics, the model recovers the underlying TMD with informative uncertainties that narrow steadily with increasing event statistics, and produces reliable estimates even with as few as 1,000 conditioning events, a statistics-limited regime directly relevant to ongoing and planned experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a conditional diffusion model to directly infer transverse momentum dependent parton distribution functions (TMD PDFs) from semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering (SIDIS) event kinematics—bypassing traditional parameterized fitting—and demonstrates robust, uncertainty-aware reconstruction even at low statistics (e.g., 1,000 events) relevant to CLAS12 and future Electron-Ion Collider experiments.
AI.motivation: Traditional TMD PDF extractions rely on fixed functional forms and iterative fitting, limiting flexibility and complicating uncertainty quantification—especially in statistics-limited regimes like current Jefferson Lab experiments.
AI.method: A conditional diffusion probabilistic model is trained to map raw SIDIS event kinematics (e.g., x, Q², z, p_T) directly to TMD PDFs (e.g., f₁(x, k_T)), learning the posterior distribution without assuming parametric forms; inference is performed via denoising sampling conditioned on observed events.
AI.result: On simulated CLAS12-like SIDIS data, the model accurately recovers ground-truth TMDs; predictive uncertainties shrink monotonically with event count; reliable TMD estimates are obtained down to ~1,000 conditioning events.
AI.conclusion: Conditional diffusion models provide a flexible, non-parametric, and uncertainty-aware framework for TMD PDF extraction—enabling more robust and statistically efficient analyses in modern nucleon structure experiments.

title: Doubly-scaled planar ${\cal N} = 4$ SYM \& Carroll Holography
summary: Okuda and Penedones (OP) \cite{Okuda:2010ym} showed the existence of a double scaling limit of four point correlators in ${\cal N}=4$ Supersymmetric Yang Mills (SYM) theory in four spacetime dimensions (4$d$) dual to the flat space limit of tree-level string amplitude in $\mathbb{R}^{1,9}$ with external kinematics in $\mathbb{R}^{1,4}$. In this paper, we show that the resulting boundary correlators can be used to define a 4d Carrollian conformal field theory (CFT) on future null infinity (${\I}^{+}$). This is done by mapping the set of correlators in ${\cal N} = 4$ SYM theory (in the double scaling limit) to ${\I}^{+}$, which is the conformal boundary of all asymptotically flat spacetimes. A Carroll CFT thus emerges in the infinite 't Hooft coupling limit of ${\cal N} = 4$ SYM theory. We extend the OP analysis to higher point functions and show how the Gram conditions on flat space amplitude put constraints on the double scaling limit of SYM correlators. We then use the soft factorization theorem for dilatonic string amplitude to write a recursion relation for $\frac{1}{2}$ BPS sector of ${\cal N} = 4$ SYM theory in the double scaling limit. Finally, we show that the essential ideas underlying such a double scaling limit can be used as a tool-kit to build a class of Carrollian correlators, and hence define a Carrollian CFT, via certain integral transforms of flat space amplitudes of non-gravitational effective field theories.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a double-scaling limit of N=4 SYM correlators that defines a 4D Carrollian CFT on future null infinity (ℐ⁺), extending Okuda–Penedones results to higher-point functions, imposing Gram constraints, deriving a soft recursion for the 1/2-BPS sector, and proposing a general integral-transform toolkit for constructing Carrollian CFTs from flat-space amplitudes.
AI.motivation: To identify and construct a Carrollian conformal field theory as an emergent boundary description of asymptotically flat spacetimes, using the flat-space limit of AdS/CFT via a controlled double-scaling limit of N=4 SYM.
AI.method: Maps N=4 SYM four- and higher-point correlators in the double-scaling ('t Hooft coupling λ→∞, momenta scaled appropriately) to ℐ⁺; imposes flat-space Gram determinant constraints on kinematics; applies soft factorization of dilatonic string amplitudes to derive recursion for 1/2-BPS correlators; introduces integral transforms from flat-space amplitudes of non-gravitational EFTs to define generic Carrollian correlators.
AI.result: Demonstrates that the OP double-scaling limit yields a well-defined 4D Carrollian CFT on ℐ⁺; derives kinematic constraints from Gram conditions for n≥5; obtains a soft recursion relation for the 1/2-BPS sector; constructs a general prescription—via Lorentz-covariant integral transforms—for generating Carrollian correlators from arbitrary flat-space amplitudes.
AI.conclusion: The double-scaling limit of N=4 SYM provides a concrete realization of a Carrollian CFT on ℐ⁺; this framework generalizes beyond string theory to effective field theories, offering a systematic method to define Carrollian dynamics from flat-space scattering data.

title: Too good to go: Upcycling Phase-Space Points for Multijet Processes
summary: The efficient sampling of high-dimensional phase spaces is a major challenge for Monte Carlo event generators, as for high-multiplicity final states the evaluation of scattering matrix elements becomes computationally expensive. We here introduce a training strategy that significantly reduces the cost of adapting the samplers, while delivering samplers that outperform the current benchmarks. The method exploits the nested structure of phase spaces, where an $(N+1)$-particle phase space factorises into an $N$-particle and a one-particle phase space. We thereby assume that an efficient sampler for the corresponding $N$-particle phase space is already available, as is the case in stacks of QCD $X+n$-jets processes. By augmenting an $N$-particle to an $(N+1)$-particle dataset, we obtain a training sample that more closely resembles the integrand and is statistically larger than, for example, a uniformly sampled one. Starting the adaptation phase of the sampler with a well-sampled $N$-particle core accelerates learning of the full $(N+1)$-particle phase-space density. Since the augmented sample is only used as an initial proposal distribution, unbiased Monte Carlo estimates are still guaranteed by exact event weighting. The approach is agnostic to the trained sampler and can be applied to machine-learning-based methods as well as more traditional algorithms such as VEGAS. We demonstrate the reduction in matrix-element evaluations and final performance increase for jet-associated Drell--Yan and top-pair production at the LHC, using Continuous Normalising Flow samplers.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a novel training strategy for Monte Carlo event generators that leverages the nested structure of phase spaces to efficiently adapt samplers for high-multiplicity final states, reducing matrix-element evaluations while maintaining unbiased sampling.
AI.motivation: Efficient sampling of high-dimensional phase spaces is computationally expensive in Monte Carlo event generation, especially for high-multiplicity final states where scattering matrix element evaluations dominate cost.
AI.method: The method exploits the factorisation of (N+1)-particle phase space into N-particle and one-particle subspaces; it augments an existing efficient N-particle sampler’s output to construct a statistically richer, integrand-aligned training set for the (N+1)-particle case, used as an initial proposal in adaptive sampling (e.g., CNF or VEGAS), with exact event weighting preserving unbiasedness.
AI.result: Demonstrated reduction in matrix-element evaluations and improved sampling efficiency for jet-associated Drell–Yan and top-pair production at the LHC using Continuous Normalising Flow samplers; outperforms current benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: The nested-phase-space augmentation strategy accelerates sampler adaptation without sacrificing statistical correctness, is sampler-agnostic, and enables scalable, high-fidelity simulation of complex collider processes.

title: Enigmatic properties of $Ξ(1620)$ and $Ξ(1690)$
summary: Motivated by a considerable release of data on first two excited states of the doubly strange baryon, $Ξ(1620)$ and $Ξ(1690)$, from different experimental collaborations in recent years, we investigate meson-baryon interactions in a coupled-channel approach. The systems are composed of pseudoscalar and vector mesons and the calculations are done for the total spin 1/2 and isospin 1/2 configuration. The tree-level interactions are deduced from Lagrangians based on chiral and hidden local symmetries. Specifically, we make an attempt to describe (1) data on the $K^-Λ$ femtoscopic correlation function coming from $p\,p$ and $Pb\,Pb$ collisions, and (2) the available data on invariant mass distributions for different systems: $πΞ$, $\bar K Σ$ and $\bar K Λ$. We find that the amplitude which yields the correlation function close to the data results in mass distributions of different meson-baryon systems that are in discordance with the experimental data and vice-versa.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates meson-baryon interactions involving doubly strange baryons Ξ(1620) and Ξ(1690) using a coupled-channel approach with chiral and hidden local symmetry Lagrangians; it finds an inconsistency between simultaneously reproducing K⁻Λ femtoscopic correlations and experimental invariant mass distributions (πΞ, K̄Σ, K̄Λ).
AI.motivation: Recent experimental data on the first two excited states of the doubly strange baryon Ξ(1620) and Ξ(1690) motivate a coupled-channel study of meson-baryon interactions to understand their nature and dynamics.
AI.method: Coupled-channel approach incorporating pseudoscalar and vector mesons with total spin 1/2 and isospin 1/2; tree-level interaction amplitudes derived from chiral and hidden local symmetry Lagrangians.
AI.result: The amplitude that best fits K⁻Λ femtoscopic correlation data (from pp and PbPb collisions) fails to reproduce experimental invariant mass distributions for πΞ, K̄Σ, and K̄Λ — and vice versa — indicating tension between these observables within the adopted theoretical framework.
AI.conclusion: Current theoretical description based on chiral + hidden local symmetry Lagrangians cannot simultaneously describe K⁻Λ femtoscopy and invariant mass spectra of relevant meson-baryon channels, suggesting limitations in the model or need for additional dynamical ingredients (e.g., higher-order terms, coupled resonant states, or improved treatment of final-state interactions).

title: Hunting long-lived doubly charged scalars at the HL-LHC
summary: This work studies the collider phenomenology of long-lived doubly charged scalars. After reviewing the existing searches for the doubly charged scalar in both the prompt and the long-lived regimes, we identify an intermediate range of proper decay length, namely, $\mathcal{O}(0.1~\mathrm{mm}) \lesssim cτ\lesssim \mathcal{O}(100~\mathrm{mm})$, where conventional searches lose sensitivity. We investigate the prospects for probing the doubly charged scalar both in the presence and in the absence of the $ΔL=2$ Yukawa coupling of the $SU(2)_{L}$ complex triplet. In the presence of this coupling, $H^{\pm\pm}$ can be long-lived only for masses in the range $100$-$150~\mathrm{GeV}$, whereas in the fermiophobic scenario (i.e., in the absence of the $ΔL=2$ coupling), the range extends to $\mathrm{TeV}$ scale. We propose a displaced-vertex search at the HL-LHC for doubly charged scalars with masses up to $\approx 1~\mathrm{TeV}$ and $cτ=10$-$100~\mathrm{mm}$ in the fermiophobic scenario, while a benchmark point with a doubly charged scalar of mass $120~\mathrm{GeV}$ and $cτ= 5~\mathrm{mm}$ is considered when the complex triplet scalar couples to leptons. We show that a cut on the invariant mass of the displaced vertex as reconstructed from the associated tracks can strongly suppress Standard Model backgrounds. We present projected limits on the Drell-Yan pair-production cross section for the doubly charged scalar at $\sqrt{s}=14~\mathrm{TeV}$ with an integrated luminosity of $3000~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$, considering two illustrative assumptions for the residual background. Displaced-vertex searches thus probe a region complementary to those covered by prompt and heavy stable charged-particle searches.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates long-lived doubly charged scalars (H±±) in an intermediate proper decay length range (0.1–100 mm) where current LHC searches lack sensitivity; it proposes displaced-vertex searches at HL-LHC for both fermiophobic (TeV-scale masses) and lepton-coupled (100–150 GeV) scenarios, demonstrating background suppression via displaced invariant mass cuts and projecting cross-section limits for 3000 fb⁻¹ at 14 TeV.
AI.motivation: Conventional prompt and heavy stable charged-particle searches are insensitive to doubly charged scalars with proper decay lengths ~0.1–100 mm; this gap motivates a dedicated displaced-vertex search strategy at the HL-LHC.
AI.method: Analyzes collider phenomenology of H±± in two scenarios: (i) with ΔL=2 Yukawa coupling (lepton-coupled, 100–150 GeV, cτ ~ 5 mm), and (ii) fermiophobic (no such coupling, up to ~1 TeV, cτ = 10–100 mm); develops a displaced-vertex search using track-based invariant mass reconstruction to suppress SM backgrounds; projects sensitivity using Drell-Yan production at √s = 14 TeV and 3000 fb⁻¹.
AI.result: A displaced-vertex search can probe H±± masses up to ~1 TeV (fermiophobic) or 120 GeV (lepton-coupled) in the intermediate cτ window; invariant mass cuts effectively suppress backgrounds; projected 95% CL cross-section limits are provided for two background assumptions.
AI.conclusion: Displaced-vertex searches at HL-LHC fill a critical sensitivity gap for long-lived doubly charged scalars, complementing existing prompt and stable-particle searches—especially in the theoretically motivated fermiophobic and low-mass lepton-coupled regimes.

title: An Axial $U_A(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$: UV Completion and Experimental Searches
summary: We propose an anomaly-free and renormalizable axial $U_A(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ model and study its experimental signatures for $A'$ masses from the MeV scale to the TeV scale. The opposite charges of the left- and right-handed charged leptons forbid the usual muon and tau Yukawa interactions. Their masses are instead generated by a singlet scalar and heavy vector-like leptons through a universal-seesaw mechanism. We focus on heavy vector-like leptons, small light--heavy mixing, and $m_s\gtrsim10~\mathrm{GeV}$. In this limit, the observables considered here depend mainly on $(m_{A'},g_X)$, while the other model parameters are restricted by mixing and perturbativity. We confront this benchmark with current experimental searches. For neutrino trident production, our finite-$m_μ$ calculation shows that $A'$ modifies the axial weak coefficient, rather than the vector coefficient relevant to the usual $L_μ-L_τ$ model. The longitudinal mode enhances muon bremsstrahlung and gives a negative contribution to $(g-2)_μ$; the latter dominates over the scalar contribution in our benchmark. Combining these results with invisible meson decays and four-muon resonance searches, we summarize the phenomenological constraints in the $(m_{A'},g_X)$ plane. For $m_{A'}\gg m_μ$, vector and axial final-state-radiation rates become nearly identical, so the corresponding collider limits can be obtained by rate matching. At a future muon collider, the total rate alone does not fully resolve the interaction structure, whereas angular distributions, especially the forward--backward asymmetry in $μ^+μ^-\toτ^+τ^-$, retain direct sensitivity to chirality.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces an anomaly-free, renormalizable axial $U_A(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ model where muon and tau masses arise via a universal seesaw involving a singlet scalar and heavy vector-like leptons; it analyzes experimental constraints (neutrino tridents, $(g-2)_μ$, meson decays, collider searches) in the $(m_{A'}, g_X)$ plane and highlights chiral sensitivity via forward–backward asymmetry at a muon collider.
AI.motivation: To construct a consistent, renormalizable extension of the Standard Model with axial $U_A(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ symmetry—avoiding anomalies and enabling light $A'$ phenomenology—while generating realistic muon and tau masses without conventional Yukawa couplings.
AI.method: Constructed an anomaly-free $U_A(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ gauge model with opposite left/right-handed lepton charges; generated charged-lepton masses via singlet scalar and vector-like leptons in a universal seesaw; performed finite-mass QED/QCD-corrected calculations for neutrino trident production, muon bremsstrahlung, $(g-2)_μ$, invisible meson decays, and $4\mu$ resonances; derived collider limits using rate matching for $m_{A'} \gg m_μ$ and analyzed angular observables (especially $A_{FB}$ in $\mu^+\mu^- \to \tau^+\tau^-$) for chiral discrimination.
AI.result: The axial nature modifies the neutrino trident amplitude by altering the axial weak coefficient (not vector); longitudinal $A'$ enhances muon bremsstrahlung and yields dominant negative contribution to $(g-2)_μ$; combined constraints exclude significant regions in the $(m_{A'}, g_X)$ plane; at high $m_{A'}$, vector/axial final-state radiation rates converge; forward–backward asymmetry in $\mu^+\mu^- \to \tau^+\tau^-$ retains definitive sensitivity to the axial coupling structure.
AI.conclusion: The axial $U_A(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ model is viable only in narrow $(m_{A'}, g_X)$ windows after current constraints; its chiral structure is not degenerate with vector models at future muon colliders, making $A_{FB}$ a robust diagnostic for axial vs. vector interactions.

title: Chiral soliton lattice in inhomogeneous magnetic fields
summary: It has been known that in sufficiently strong uniform magnetic fields, the ground state of quantum chromodynamics (QCD) supports a spatially modulated condensate of neutral pions, dubbed chiral soliton lattice (CSL). In this paper, we investigate whether a similar ordered ground state might exist when the external magnetic field is nonuniform, as appropriate for potential phenomenological applications, including heavy-ion collisions and neutron stars. To that end, we use the low-energy effective field theory of QCD, restricted to the neutral pions as the sole low-energy degrees of freedom in strong magnetic fields. In the limit of vanishing pion mass, we achieve a complete characterization of magnetic fields supporting a CSL-like ground state. Moreover, for a simple but infinite family of magnetic fields, we find the corresponding CSL state analytically. Going away from the massless limit requires full numerical minimization of the energy functional. Here we provide some sample numerical results, focusing on the qualitative differences as compared to the situations with a uniform magnetic field or a vanishing pion mass. The main conclusion remains unchanged: while bending the magnetic field typically reduces the energy gain due to the neutral pion condensation, a CSL-type ground state is still possible. As a byproduct of our work, we map the location of the CSL phase in the phase diagram of QCD in a uniform magnetic field and finite volume.

Using the low-energy effective theory of QCD with neutral pions only, it analytically characterizes CSL-supporting fields in the massless pion limit, solves for CSL solutions in an infinite family of nonuniform fields, and numerically studies massive-pion cases. Results show CSL remains viable under field inhomogeneity, albeit with reduced energy gain; the work also maps the CSL phase in the uniform-field, finite-volume QCD phase diagram.
AI.motivation: To determine whether the chiral soliton lattice (CSL), previously established in uniform strong magnetic fields, can survive under realistic nonuniform magnetic fields—e.g., those in heavy-ion collisions and magnetized neutron stars—thereby extending its phenomenological relevance.

AI.conclusion: The chiral soliton lattice is robust against magnetic field inhomogeneity: while field bending suppresses the energetic advantage of pion condensation, a CSL-type ground state remains thermodynamically viable in physically relevant nonuniform magnetic environments.
